title.zh: 卷451 列傳二百三十八 李朝仪 段起 丁寿昌 曾纪凤 储裕立 铁珊 桂中行 刘含芳 陈黉举 遊智开 李用清 李希莲 李金镛 金福曾 熊其英 谢家福 童兆蓉
title.en: Volume 451 Biographies 238: Li Chaoyi, Duan Qi, Ding Shouchang, Ceng Jifeng, Chu Yuli, Tie Shan, Gui Zhonghang, Liu Hanfang, Chen Hongju, You Zhi Kai, Li Yongqing, Li Xilian, Li Jinyong, Jin Fuceng, Xiong Qiying, Xie Jiafu, Tong Zhaorong
title.raw: 卷451 列傳二百三十八 李朝仪 段起 丁寿昌 曾纪凤 储裕立 铁珊 桂中行 刘含芳 陈黉举 遊智开 李用清 李希莲 李金镛 金福曾 熊其英 谢家福 童兆蓉

sentences.zh: 李朝儀，字藻舟，貴州貴築人。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyi, styled Zaozhou, was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyi, whose courtesy name was Zaozhou, came from Guizhu in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，授直隸平谷縣，歷署饒陽、三河。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi and was appointed to Pinggu County in Zhili; he successively served as acting magistrate of Raoyang and Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Daoguang reign and was posted as magistrate of Pinggu in Zhili, later serving in acting charge of Raoyang and Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，遷大興京縣，署南路同知，補東路同知，皆有治聲。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he was transferred to Daxing Jing County, served as acting subprefect of the Southern Circuit, and was then appointed subprefect of the Eastern Circuit; in each post he had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng era he was moved to Daxing Jing County, acted as subprefect of the Southern Circuit, and then took the Eastern Circuit post permanently, winning praise for sound administration in every assignment.

sentences.zh: 時海防戒嚴，築寧河、北塘、大沽諸砲台，工堅費核，平餘銀鉅萬，悉以入官，晉秩知府。

translations.literal: When coastal defense was on alert, he built batteries at Ninghe, Beitang, Dagu, and elsewhere; the works were solid and expenses were audited, and a surplus of tens of thousands of taels he turned over entirely to the government, and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: While coastal defenses were on high alert, he oversaw batteries at Ninghe, Beitang, Dagu, and other sites. The fortifications were sturdily built and costs tightly checked; a surplus of many tens of thousands of taels he handed over in full to the treasury, and he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 十年，署順德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting magistrate of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the reign he acted as magistrate of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 捻匪北竄，朝儀率鄉勇出禦，嚴陣以待，砲折大旗，迄不動。

translations.literal: Nian bandits fled north; Chaoyi led local militia out to resist, drew up a strict formation and waited; cannon shot broke the great banner, yet they did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian rebels drove north, Chaoyi led local militia to meet them. He held his men in tight formation; though artillery shattered the main banner, the line never broke.

sentences.zh: 益使遊騎左右馳突為疑兵，賊來則擊之，退則寂守，久之，賊引去。

translations.literal: He further sent mounted scouts to charge left and right as decoys; when the bandits came he struck them, and when they withdrew he held silently; after a long time the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent mounted scouts to wheel about on both flanks as a feint: strike when the enemy advanced, hold quietly when they fell back. In time the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，署廣平，敗賊馬甿橋，悉收難民入城，料賊必復至，儲糧械為城守備。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he served as acting magistrate of Guangping, defeated bandits at Ma'eng Bridge, gathered all refugees into the city, reckoned the bandits would return, and stored grain and weapons for the city's defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he acted at Guangping, routed the enemy at Ma'eng Bridge, brought every refugee inside the walls, and—expecting another attack—stockpiled grain and arms for a siege.

sentences.zh: 已而賊眾數万果逼城，不敢犯，城獲全。

translations.literal: Before long tens of thousands of bandits did press the city but dared not attack, and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Soon tens of thousands of rebels did surround the city, but they dared not assault it, and the town was saved.

sentences.zh: 五年，補大名。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed magistrate of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received a permanent appointment as magistrate of Daming.

sentences.zh: 馬學孟者，故捻黨也，善戰，有勇力。

translations.literal: Ma Xuemeng had formerly been of the Nian party, was skilled in warfare, and had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xuemeng had once been a Nian rebel—an able fighter, bold and strong.

sentences.zh: 既投誠，充團總，濬、滑、內黃數縣民多附之，其黨有殺人者，遠近因傳學孟叛矣。

translations.literal: After he submitted in good faith he served as militia chief; people of Jun, Hua, and Neihuang counties and others largely attached to him; among his followers were killers, and far and near therefore spread word that Xuemeng had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After he surrendered he became a militia captain, and many people in Jun, Hua, Neihuang, and neighboring counties rallied to him. Some of his men committed murder, and rumor soon spread that Xuemeng had turned rebel again.

sentences.zh: 朝儀馳入其居，曉譬利害，學孟悟而泣，原繳械請罪，遂夷其寨，赦勿問。

translations.literal: Chaoyi galloped to his dwelling, explained the advantages and harms; Xuemeng came to understanding and wept, wished to surrender weapons and beg forgiveness; he then leveled the stockade and pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi rode straight to his home and reasoned with him about the stakes. Xuemeng broke down in tears, offered to turn in his arms and accept punishment; Chaoyi dismantled the stronghold and granted a full pardon.

sentences.zh: 後朝儀與賊戰，得學孟死力，故不敗。

translations.literal: Later when Chaoyi fought bandits he obtained Xuemeng's utmost effort, and therefore did not suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in battles with the rebels, Chaoyi had Xuemeng's unstinting service—and so never lost.

sentences.zh: 八年，授永定河道，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed commissioner of the Yongding River course and served as acting provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was named commissioner of the Yongding River and acted as provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 先後任河道八年，勤於職守，痛革河工積弊，課兵種柳，資工用焉。

translations.literal: He successively held the river post for eight years, was diligent in duty, bitterly reformed long-standing abuses in river works, set soldiers to planting willows, and used them to supply labor needs.
translations.idiomatic: He held river office for eight years in all, worked tirelessly, and rooted out entrenched corruption in hydraulic projects. He had troops plant willows to supply materials for the works.

sentences.zh: 遷山東鹽運使，尋擢順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shandong salt transport commissioner, and soon promoted to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Shandong salt commissioner, then soon elevated to Intendant of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 京畿靡薄，朝儀廉勤率之，捕劇盜，抑豪強，絕請託，期年風習一變。

translations.literal: The capital region was dissolute; Chaoyi led with integrity and diligence, captured notorious robbers, curbed powerful families, cut off solicitations, and within a year customs changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The capital district had grown lax; Chaoyi led by example with integrity and industry, arrested notorious bandits, checked the mighty, and refused every favor—within a year the whole tone of the region had shifted.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the seventh year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 朝儀治河績尤著，民立祠固安祀之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi's achievements in governing the river were especially outstanding; the people erected a shrine at Gu'an to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: His record on the rivers was especially distinguished; the people raised a shrine at Gu'an in his honor.

sentences.zh: 段起，字小湖，湖南清泉人。

translations.literal: Duan Qi, styled Xiaohu, was a native of Qingquan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Qi, courtesy name Xiaohu, was from Qingquan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初入貲助餉，敘道員。

translations.literal: At first he contributed funds to aid military pay and was ranked as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first gained rank as a circuit intendant by donating funds for army provisions.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，佐廣西左江道王普相幕，數陳兵事。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he assisted in the staff of Wang Puxiang, Left River Circuit of Guangxi, and repeatedly presented military plans.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he joined the staff of Wang Puxiang, the Left River intendant of Guangxi, and often submitted plans for the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 普相薦諸巡撫勞崇光，俾將百人，從解全州圍。

translations.literal: Puxiang recommended him to Governor La Chongguang, had him command a hundred men, and followed in relieving the siege of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Puxiang recommended him to Governor La Chongguang, who gave him command of a hundred men to help lift the siege of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 別寇鄧正高乘虛襲永州，窺衡州，起單騎馳諭降其眾。

translations.literal: Another bandit, Deng Zhenggao, seized the opportunity to strike Yongzhou and eyed Hengzhou; Qi alone on horseback galloped to persuade and reduce his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel leader, Deng Zhenggao, struck at Yongzhou and menaced Hengzhou. Qi rode in alone and talked his followers into surrender.

sentences.zh: 貴州叛苗犯懷遠，起討平之。

translations.literal: Rebel Miao in Guizhou invaded Huaiyuan; Qi campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou Miao rebels attacked Huaiyuan, Qi marched against them and restored order.

sentences.zh: 奉檄率所部援江西，謁曾國籓於軍中，國籓未之奇也。

translations.literal: By order he led his troops to aid Jiangxi and called on Zeng Guofan in camp; Guofan did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Jiangxi with his troops, he presented himself to Zeng Guofan in camp—but Zeng was not impressed.

sentences.zh: 時賊踞建昌，久不下。

translations.literal: At the time bandits held Jianchang and it had long not been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Jianchang, and the city had long resisted capture.

sentences.zh: 起夜率四百人撲其壘，克之，乘勝复德安，國籓乃納其軍。

translations.literal: By night Qi led four hundred men to storm their fort, took it, and following victory recovered De'an; Guofan then accepted his army.
translations.idiomatic: Qi led four hundred men in a night assault on their camp, took it, and pressed on to recover De'an. Only then did Zeng take his force into his own command.

sentences.zh: 七年，從劉騰鴻、李續宜攻瑞州，騰鴻戰死，起亦被重創，卒克之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Liu Tenghong and Li Xuyi in attacking Ruizhou; Tenghong died in battle and Qi also received grave wounds, but in the end they took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Liu Tenghong and Li Xuyi in the assault on Ruizhou. Tenghong fell in battle and Qi was badly wounded, but the city was taken in the end.

sentences.zh: 八年，援浙，解衢州圍，還攻景德、浮梁，並克之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he aided Zhejiang, relieved the siege of Quzhou, returned to attack Jingde and Fuliang, and took both.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he went to aid Zhejiang, broke the siege of Quzhou, then turned back to take Jingde and Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，陳玉成犯景德，起扼其衝，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: The next year Chen Yucheng invaded Jingde; Qi blocked his route and the bandits could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Chen Yucheng struck at Jingde, Qi held the choke point and the rebels could not break through.

sentences.zh: 出家財募勇，遣別將率以援浙，數有功。

translations.literal: He spent family wealth to recruit braves, sent another general to lead them to aid Zhejiang, and repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own money to raise troops and sent a subordinate with them to Zhejiang, where they won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王有齡疏調起赴浙將水陸軍，會以前功加鹽運使銜，留江西以道員補用。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Youling memorialized to transfer Qi to Zhejiang to command land and water forces; coinciding with earlier merit he was given the rank of salt transport commissioner, but was kept in Jiangxi to fill a circuit intendant post.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Youling asked that Qi be sent to Zhejiang to command combined land and river forces. For his earlier service he received the salt-commissioner rank, but he remained in Jiangxi as a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，李秀成犯廣豐，遂圍廣信。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Li Xiucheng invaded Guangfeng and then besieged Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Li Xiucheng attacked Guangfeng and then laid siege to Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 起嬰城固守，伺間出擊賊，敗之，賊遂引去，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Qi tied himself to the city and held firm, watched for an opening to sally and strike the bandits, defeated them, and the bandits then withdrew; he was given the rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Qi defended the walled city stubbornly, sallied when he saw an opening, routed the enemy, and the rebels withdrew. He was awarded the provincial treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，授江西督糧道，仍留治軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed Jiangxi grain-supply commissioner but still remained to manage the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was named Jiangxi grain commissioner while continuing to command troops.

sentences.zh: 二年，克鄱陽、彭澤，給瑚松額巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: In the second year he took Poyang and Pengze and was given the title of Baturu Hüsonggo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he captured Poyang and Pengze and received the Baturu title Hüsonggo.

sentences.zh: 三年，始赴任。

translations.literal: In the third year he first went to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the third year did he take up the civil post in person.

sentences.zh: 時軍事漸定，議撤兵。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs were gradually settling and there was discussion of disbanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting was winding down, and officials debated demobilization.

sentences.zh: 起條上兵弁安置之策，巡撫沈葆楨疏請頒行，武職借補及收標考課，著為令。

translations.literal: Qi itemized policies for settling officers and men; Governor Shen Baozhen memorialized to promulgate them, and provisional appointment of military posts and intake, rostering, and examination were established as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Qi drew up a detailed plan for placing officers and soldiers after demobilization. Governor Shen Baozhen memorialized for its adoption, and rules on provisional military appointments, mustering, and examinations were codified.

sentences.zh: 四年，鮑超軍索餉譁潰，起聞變馳視，遇前隊，傷頤，有識者大呼曰：「段糧道也！」

translations.literal: In the fourth year Bao Chao's army clamored for pay and mutinied and dispersed; Qi heard of the disturbance and galloped to look; he met the vanguard, was wounded on the cheek, and someone who knew him shouted, 'It is Grain Commissioner Duan!'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Bao Chao's troops mutinied over unpaid wages. Qi rode to the scene at once, ran into the vanguard, and was struck in the face. Someone who knew him cried out, 'It is Commissioner Duan of the grain bureau!'

sentences.zh: 皆棄兵拜，起反覆開譬，變乃定。

translations.literal: All cast down weapons and bowed; Qi repeatedly explained and admonished, and the disturbance was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The men dropped their weapons and bowed. Qi reasoned with them at length until the riot subsided.

sentences.zh: 尋兼署按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as acting provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted concurrently as provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 江西、閩、浙之交，有山綿亙千里，故為盜藪，久封禁。

translations.literal: At the junction of Jiangxi, Fujian, and Zhejiang there were mountains stretching a thousand li, formerly a haunt of bandits, long closed and forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Where Jiangxi, Fujian, and Zhejiang meet, mountains run for a thousand li—a former bandit refuge that had long been closed to settlement.

sentences.zh: 賊未平時，民往往入山避亂，久之生息日繁。

translations.literal: Before the bandits were pacified the people often entered the mountains to escape disorder; after a long time their livelihoods daily grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: While rebellion still raged, refugees had often fled into those hills; in time their numbers grew.

sentences.zh: 至是或頗言粵寇餘孽窟穴其中，詔三省會剿，起疑之，輕騎週曆詢訪，悉其狀，牒大吏疏請弛禁，民德之，立生祠祀焉。

translations.literal: By then some spoke much of Guangdong bandit remnants harbored there; an edict ordered the three provinces to join in suppression; Qi doubted this, with light cavalry made a circuit of inquiry and visits, learned the full situation, and memorialized through superiors to request lifting the ban; the people were grateful and erected a living shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Now some claimed Taiping remnants were hiding there, and the throne ordered a joint campaign by three provinces. Qi was skeptical; he toured the region on horseback, learned the truth, and petitioned to reopen the mountains. Grateful settlers raised a shrine to him while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went home ill.

sentences.zh: 邑大饑，傾貲賑贍，全活逾萬家。

translations.literal: The district suffered great famine; he poured out wealth for relief and sustenance, and preserved alive more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck his home district, he spent his fortune on relief and saved more than ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，再授江西督糧道，調江南徐州道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was again appointed Jiangxi grain commissioner and was transferred to Xuzhou Circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he was again named Jiangxi grain commissioner, then transferred to the Xuzhou circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 六年，兩廣總督張樹聲調治海防，擢廣東鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Governor-General Zhang Shusheng of Liangguang transferred him to manage coastal defense, and he was promoted to Guangdong salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhang Shusheng, governor-general of Liangguang, put him in charge of coastal defense and promoted him to Guangdong salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 丁壽昌，字樂山，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Ding Shouchang, styled Leshan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shouchang, courtesy name Leshan, was from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少為裡塾師，粵寇擾淮南，遂集里中子弟勒以兵法，築寨自保。

translations.literal: In youth he was a village schoolteacher; when Guangdong bandits disturbed Huainan, he then gathered local youths and drilled them in military methods, built a stockade, and protected themselves.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he taught in a village school. When the Taiping rebellion swept Huainan, he gathered local youths, trained them in tactics, and built a fortified camp for their defense.

sentences.zh: 同治初，率偏師從李鴻章東征，轉戰蘇、松間，由知縣晉秩知府。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi he led a detached force following Li Hongzhang east in campaign, fought back and forth between Suzhou and Songjiang, and rose from magistrate to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he led a detachment under Li Hongzhang's eastern campaigns, fighting across Suzhou and Songjiang, and rose from magistrate to prefect.

sentences.zh: 隨潘鼎新攻浙江，克乍浦，攝乍浦同知。

translations.literal: He followed Pan Dingxin in attacking Zhejiang, took Zhapu, and acted as Zhapu subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: With Pan Dingxin he campaigned in Zhejiang, captured Zhapu, and served as acting subprefect there.

sentences.zh: 又隨克嘉興，晉道員。

translations.literal: He again followed in taking Jiaxing and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped take Jiaxing and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 進攻湖州，戰於晟舍鎮，賊憑河為險。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Huzhou, they fought at Shenshe Town; the bandits relied on the river as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Huzhou they fought at Shenshe, where the rebels used the river as their defense.

sentences.zh: 壽昌鳧水破其兩壘，諸軍隨擊，立克之，湖州賊遂不振。

translations.literal: Shouchang swam the water and broke their two forts; the various armies followed in attack and quickly took them; the Huzhou bandits then did not recover strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang swam the river and stormed two enemy forts; the main force followed and carried the day, and the rebels at Huzhou never recovered.

sentences.zh: 論功，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was given the rank of provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the provincial judge rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，率師從劉銘傳剿捻，迭敗之黃安、鄧州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led troops following Liu Mingchuan in suppressing the Nian, and repeatedly defeated them at Huang'an and Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he campaigned with Liu Mingchuan against the Nian, defeating them repeatedly at Huang'an and Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊南竄沭陽，霖雨，平地水數尺，捻酋任化邦竄渡沭水而西。

translations.literal: The bandits fled south to Shuyang; incessant rain left several feet of water on level ground; the Nian chief Ren Huabang fled crossing the Shu River westward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled south toward Shuyang. Heavy rains left several feet of water on the plain, and Nian chief Ren Huabang slipped across the Shu River to the west.

sentences.zh: 壽昌先解衣率將士徒涉，伐木為梁濟軍，既濟，乃斷梁。

translations.literal: Shouchang first removed his clothes and led officers and soldiers to wade across, felled trees to make a bridge to ferry the army, and after crossing then cut the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang stripped and waded across first with his men, then felled trees for a bridge to bring the army over—and cut the bridge behind them once they had crossed.

sentences.zh: 眾知無退路，奮擊破賊，追斬化邦贛榆城下。

translations.literal: The troops knew there was no retreat, fought fiercely and broke the bandits, pursued and beheaded Huabang below Ganyu city.
translations.idiomatic: With no way back, the men fought desperately, routed the enemy, and ran down Ren Huabang beneath the walls of Ganyu.

sentences.zh: 詔以道員簡放，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: By edict he was selected and released as circuit intendant and given the rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a regular circuit intendant by imperial order and given the provincial treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 又戰濰縣，擒捻酋李芸等，給西林巴圖魯勇號，記名按察使。

translations.literal: He again fought at Weixian, captured Nian chiefs Li Yun and others, was given the brave title of Baturu Xilin, and was registered by name as provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: At Weixian he captured Nian leaders including Li Yun, received the Baturu title Xilin, and was placed on the register for provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 八年，天津民、教構釁，命壽昌率銘軍四千馳赴津、沽備非常。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Tianjin commoners and missionaries provoked an incident; Shouchang was ordered to lead four thousand men of the Ming army to gallop to Tianjin and the coast to guard against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Tianjin massacre inflamed tensions; Shouchang was ordered to rush four thousand Ming-brigade troops to Tianjin and the coast against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 遂署天津道，尋實授。

translations.literal: He then served as acting Tianjin circuit intendant and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as Tianjin circuit intendant and soon received the post in full.

sentences.zh: 時人情洶懼，譌言繁興。

translations.literal: At the time popular feeling was turbulent and fearful, and false rumors flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Panic ran high and rumors multiplied.

sentences.zh: 壽昌處以鎮靜，扶良詰姦，屬境安堵。

translations.literal: Shouchang met it with calm, supported the good and examined the wicked, and the jurisdiction was peaceful and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchang kept his composure, protected the law-abiding and pursued wrongdoers, and the district grew calm.

sentences.zh: 救火會董積憤西教，適大火，相約不救教堂。

translations.literal: The directors of the fire brigade harbored accumulated resentment against Western teaching; just then a great fire broke out, and they agreed not to save the church.
translations.idiomatic: The fire-company leaders nursed a grudge against Western missionaries. When a major blaze broke out, they agreed among themselves not to fight the church fire.

sentences.zh: 壽昌聞警奔赴，略無畛域。

translations.literal: Shouchang heard the alarm and rushed there, with no distinction of boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Shouchang raced to the scene and showed no partiality whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 會董感其誠，乃施救。

translations.literal: The directors were moved by his sincerity and then undertook rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his sincerity, the fire-company leaders joined the rescue after all.

sentences.zh: 梁家園河堤將圮，壽昌親執畚立水中，眾益奮築，堤獲全。

translations.literal: The Liangjiayuan river embankment was about to collapse; Shouchang personally took a basket and stood in the water; the crowd was all the more zealous in building, and the dike was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liangjiayuan dike began to give way, Shouchang took a basket himself and stood in the water; the workers redoubled their efforts and the embankment held.

sentences.zh: 設廠以賑流民，廬灶籓溷悉有程式。

translations.literal: He established relief sheds for displaced people; huts, kitchens, latrines, and fences all had set regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He set up relief camps for refugees, with fixed standards for shelters, kitchens, and sanitation.

sentences.zh: 會遭父喪，士民奔走籥留者萬人，堅請終制。

translations.literal: He then suffered his father's death; scholars and commoners numbering ten thousand ran about pleading with pipes to detain him, firmly asking him to complete mourning on site.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, ten thousand townspeople begged him to stay and complete mourning there rather than leave office.

sentences.zh: 服除，詔赴天津總理營務，兼充海防翼長。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, by edict he went to Tianjin to manage camp affairs in general and concurrently served as assistant chief of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was ordered to Tianjin to oversee military camps and to serve concurrently as deputy chief of coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，署津海關道，擢按察使，署布政使，以勤慎稱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he served as acting Jinghai customs circuit intendant, was promoted to provincial judge, acted as provincial treasurer, and was known for diligence and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he acted as Jinghai customs intendant, was promoted to provincial judge, and served as acting provincial treasurer, earning a name for diligence and care.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，贈太常卿，於天津建立專祠。

translations.literal: Grants of condolence were given, he was posthumously made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, and a dedicated shrine was established at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted condolence gifts, posthumously made him Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, and ordered a private shrine built for him at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 曾紀鳳，字摯民，湖南邵陽人。

translations.literal: Ceng Jifeng, styled Zhimin, was a native of Shaoyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Jifeng, courtesy name Zhimin, was from Shaoyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以諸生從軍，洊保知縣。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he followed the army and was repeatedly recommended to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate who took up arms, he was repeatedly recommended for magistrate rank.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章督四川，調領湘果後營。

translations.literal: When Luo Bingzhang governed Sichuan, he was transferred to command the rear camp of the Xiang Guo army.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang was governor of Sichuan, Jifeng was assigned to lead the rear battalion of the Hunan army.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，石達開竄踞敘州雙龍場，分軍陷高縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Shi Dakai fled and occupied Shuanglongchang at Xuzhou, and detached troops took Gaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, Shi Dakai seized Shuanglongchang in Xuzhou and sent columns to take Gaoxian.

sentences.zh: 紀鳳從按察使劉岳昭赴援，戰城下，克之。

translations.literal: Jifeng followed Provincial Judge Liu Yuezhao to the relief, fought below the city, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Jifeng marched with Provincial Judge Liu Yuezhao to relieve the city, fought beneath the walls, and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 又迭敗之吊黃樓、羅家坳，涉水先驅奪賊壘。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly defeated them at Diaohuanglou and Luojia'ao, waded water as vanguard, and seized bandit forts.
translations.idiomatic: He won further victories at Diaohuanglou and Luojia'ao, wading rivers at the head of the column to storm rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 達開連營三十，與橫江為犄角。

translations.literal: Dakai had thirty linked camps forming a horn with the Heng River.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai held thirty linked camps, using the Heng River as a defensive angle.

sentences.zh: 紀鳳毀橫江西岸賊巢，遂薄雙龍場。

translations.literal: Jifeng destroyed bandit nests on the west bank of the Heng River and then pressed close to Shuanglongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jifeng destroyed rebel bases on the west bank of the Heng, then closed on Shuanglongchang.

sentences.zh: 計招賊黨為內應，而潛軍襲其後。

translations.literal: He planned to recruit bandit partisans as inside collaborators while secretly sending troops to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: He won over enemy collaborators inside the camp while sending troops in a stealth attack from the rear.

sentences.zh: 達開奔燕子灘，邀於橫河，半渡，擊之，遂竄滇境。

translations.literal: Dakai fled to Yanzitan; they intercepted him at the Heng River, struck when he was half across, and he then fled into Yunnan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai fled toward Yanzitan; Jifeng intercepted him on the Heng and struck while his force was mid-crossing, driving him into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三年，從克正安，進圍綏陽，屢戰有功，晉知府。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in taking Zheng'an, advanced to besiege Suiyang, repeatedly fought with merit, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he helped take Zheng'an and besiege Suiyang, fought with distinction, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣東，又調貴州，並任軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guangdong, then again to Guizhou, in each place holding military duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Guangdong, then to Guizhou, holding military command in both.

sentences.zh: 十年，與總兵鄧千勝克麻哈，擒楊阿保，晉道員。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, together with Brigadier Deng Qiansheng, he took Mahu, captured Yang Abao, and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he and Brigadier Deng Qiansheng took Mahu, captured Yang Abao, and he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會諸軍剿平苗民之梗化者。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he joined various armies in suppressing and pacifying recalcitrant Miao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined allied forces in pacifying rebellious Miao.

sentences.zh: 貴州下游東西驛道，苗在其南，漢民在其北。

translations.literal: On the east-west courier route in lower Guizhou, Miao were to its south and Han people to its north.
translations.idiomatic: On the east-west post road in lower Guizhou, Miao lived to the south and Han settlers to the north.

sentences.zh: 自咸豐時，行旅阻隔，垂二十年，至是始通。

translations.literal: Since the Xianfeng era travelers had been blocked; for nearly twenty years, until now it was first opened.
translations.idiomatic: Travel on the route had been cut off since Xianfeng—nearly twenty years—until now it opened again.

sentences.zh: 紀鳳辦理善後，自黃平以上歷清平、平越、麻哈、貴定二百餘裡，建碉七十，分立四屯，各設屯官，戍卒六百分守之。

translations.literal: Jifeng handled aftermath affairs; from Huangping upward through Qingping, Pingyue, Mahu, and Guiding for more than two hundred li he built seventy blockhouses, established four separate garrison colonies, each with a colony officer, and six hundred garrison soldiers divided to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Jifeng managed the pacification: along more than two hundred li from Huangping through Qingping, Pingyue, Mahu, and Guiding he built seventy blockhouses, organized four garrison districts each with its own officer, and stationed six hundred troops to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 墾荒供餉，責以巡緝。

translations.literal: They reclaimed wasteland to supply provisions and were charged with patrol and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons reclaimed land to feed themselves and were charged with patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 姦宄無所容，流民聞風踵至。

translations.literal: Evildoers had nowhere to hide, and displaced people hearing the report came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongdoers found no refuge, and refugees flocked in upon hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 十二年，古州苗叛，擾清江，旁寨響應。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Miao of Guzhou rebelled, disturbed Qingjiang, and neighboring stockades responded in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Guzhou Miao rose, raided Qingjiang, and neighboring villages joined them.

sentences.zh: 紀鳳率碉兵會諸軍進剿，擒其酋長，撫良苗百數十寨。

translations.literal: Jifeng led blockhouse soldiers and joined various armies in advancing to suppress, captured their chieftains, and pacified good Miao in more than a hundred and several tens of stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Jifeng led garrison troops from the blockhouses in a joint campaign, captured the rebel chiefs, and brought more than a hundred loyal Miao villages back under control.

sentences.zh: 黔疆略定，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The Guizhou frontier was largely settled, and he was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: With the Guizhou frontier largely pacified, he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授貴西道，巡撫黎培敬深倚之，薦可大用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed Guixi Circuit intendant; Governor Li Peijing relied on him deeply and recommended him as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was named intendant of Guixi Circuit. Governor Li Peijing relied on him heavily and recommended him for higher office.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，晉布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge and advanced to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial judge, then to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調雲南布政使，剿倮黑及大戛寨夷，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Yunnan provincial treasurer, suppressed the Luoblack and the Yi of Dajia Stockade, and was given the first-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Yunnan as provincial treasurer, campaigned against the Luoblack and Yi of Dajia Stockade, and received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 因請以其地改土歸流，邊隅以安。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that those lands be converted from native rule to regular administration, and the border regions were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to replace native chieftain rule with regular administration, and the frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十五年，乞養歸，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he begged leave to return home to support his parents, and soon after died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he retired to care for his parents and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 儲裕立，字鶴樵，湖南靖州人。

translations.literal: Chu Yuli, styled Heqiao, was a native of Jingzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuli, courtesy name Heqiao, was from Jingzhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 從軍貴州，累保知縣。

translations.literal: He followed the army in Guizhou and was repeatedly recommended to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Guizhou campaigns and was repeatedly recommended for magistrate rank.

sentences.zh: 同治初，苗亂熾，迭克天柱、清江，晉知府。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi the Miao rebellion flared; he repeatedly took Tianzhu and Qingjiang and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, as the Miao rebellion raged, he captured Tianzhu and Qingjiang in succession and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 十年，署古州同知。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting subprefect of Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he acted as subprefect of Guzhou.

sentences.zh: 兵後彫攰，群苗伺釁出沒。

translations.literal: After the troops departed the land was devastated; Miao bands watched for openings and came and went raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The region lay in ruins after the fighting, and Miao bands lurked nearby, raiding whenever they saw an opening.

sentences.zh: 裕立修戰備，撫遺黎，民氣漸復。

translations.literal: Yuli repaired war preparations, comforted the survivors, and popular morale gradually recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli restored defenses, comforted the survivors, and gradually revived the people's spirits.

sentences.zh: 仍統軍先後收復台拱、丹江、凱里諸城，擢道員。

translations.literal: Still commanding troops, he successively recovered Taigong, Danjiang, Kaili, and other cities, and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Still in command, he recovered Taigong, Danjiang, Kaili, and other towns in turn and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，下游肅清，論功，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu the lower reaches were pacified; discussing merit, he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu the lower Guizhou region was cleared; for his service he received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 督治善後，築城堡百二十七，建義塾百三十九。

translations.literal: He supervised aftermath administration, built 127 fortresses and castles, and established 139 charity schools.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw reconstruction, building 127 fortresses and founding 139 charity schools.

sentences.zh: 八年，思南災，裕立往賑，遍歷災區，日稽錢粟出入，無假借，實惠及民。

translations.literal: In the eighth year there was disaster at Sinan; Yuli went for relief, made a circuit of the disaster area, daily examined money and grain in and out, allowed no misappropriation, and real benefit reached the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Sinan suffered disaster, Yuli went to administer relief. He toured every affected area, audited grain and funds daily without favor, and saw that aid reached the people.

sentences.zh: 時遵義焚教堂，民情洶洶。

translations.literal: At the time Zunyi burned a church and popular feeling was turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: About then a church was burned at Zunyi and public feeling ran high.

sentences.zh: 裕立馳往撫諭，與法人往復詰難，事得解。

translations.literal: Yuli galloped there to soothe and instruct, argued back and forth with the French, and the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli rushed there to calm the people and debated the matter with the French until the crisis was settled.

sentences.zh: 尋署貴西道，再歷貴東糧儲。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting Guixi circuit intendant and again held Guidong grain and storage duties.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as Guixi intendant and later held the Guidong grain-supply post again.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; condolence grants were given according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year and received the usual condolence grants.

sentences.zh: 鐵珊，字紹裴，徐氏，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Tie Shan, styled Shaopei, of the Xu clan, was a bondservant of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Shan, courtesy name Shaopei, of the Xu clan, was a Han bondservant of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，由筆帖式議敘知縣。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng, from clerk of the Grand Secretariat he was ranked by merit discussion to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era he rose from Grand Secretariat clerk to magistrate by merit.

sentences.zh: 從欽差大臣勝保討捻山東，單騎入賊壘，招降捻匪劉占考，散其黨數万。

translations.literal: He followed Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao in suppressing the Nian in Shandong, alone on horseback entered the bandit camp, induced the Nian bandit Liu Zhankao to surrender, and dispersed his followers numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: With Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao he campaigned against the Nian in Shandong, rode alone into the enemy camp, persuaded Nian leader Liu Zhankao to surrender, and disbanded tens of thousands of his followers.

sentences.zh: 敘功，以直隸州選用。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was selected for use as a Zhili department magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed a department magistrate in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同治初，發甘肅，署通渭。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi he was sent to Gansu and served as acting magistrate of Tongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he was posted to Gansu as acting magistrate of Tongwei.

sentences.zh: 值回亂，一歲九被圍，嬰城固守，卒得全。

translations.literal: He encountered the Muslim rebellion; in one year the city was besieged nine times; he tied himself to the city and held firm, and in the end it was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: During the Muslim uprising the city was besieged nine times in a single year. He held the walls stubbornly and the town survived.

sentences.zh: 日供軍糧萬斤，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Each day ten thousand jin of army grain were supplied, and the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The army demanded ten thousand jin of grain a day, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 鐵珊規減其半，民感德。

translations.literal: Tie Shan planned to reduce it by half, and the people were grateful for his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Shan cut the levy in half, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 及去任，攀轅不得行。

translations.literal: When he left his post, they clung to his carriage shafts and he could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, the people clung to his carriage and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 迭攝平番、皋蘭、中衛諸邑，所至輒輕賦役，輯流亡，修城堡，除蠹胥。

translations.literal: He successively acted at Pingfan, Gaolan, Zhongwei, and other districts; wherever he arrived he promptly lightened taxes and corvée, gathered displaced people, repaired castles and walls, and removed corrupt clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn at Pingfan, Gaolan, Zhongwei, and other posts. Everywhere he went he eased taxes and labor service, resettled refugees, repaired fortifications, and purged corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 總督上其治狀，擢寧夏知府，未之任，調蘭州。

translations.literal: The governor-general reported his record of governance; he was promoted to Ningxia prefect but did not take up the post and was transferred to Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general reported his achievements; he was promoted to prefect of Ningxia but was transferred to Lanzhou before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 議建貢院，與陝西分試，自光緒紀元始。

translations.literal: He proposed building an examination hall and holding separate examinations with Shaanxi, beginning from the first year of the Guangxu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building an examination hall so Gansu could hold provincial exams separately from Shaanxi, beginning in the first year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 是年，署甘涼道，武威、永昌、鎮番三邑​​共一渠，民爭水械鬥，久不決。

translations.literal: That year he served as acting Ganliang circuit intendant; Wuwei, Yongchang, and Zhenfan three districts shared one canal; the people fought over water with weapons and the dispute long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as acting intendant of Ganliang, he faced a long-standing feud: Wuwei, Yongchang, and Zhenfan shared one canal, and farmers fought over water with weapons.

sentences.zh: 鐵珊為開支渠，別子母水，設徬刊石，立均水約，輪日灌溉，民大悅，為立祠渠上。

translations.literal: Tie Shan opened branch canals, separated main and branch water, set markers and carved stone inscriptions, established an equal-water covenant, and rotated irrigation by day; the people were greatly pleased and erected a shrine for him above the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Shan dug branch canals, divided main and subsidiary flows, set stone markers, drew up a water-sharing agreement with rotation by day, and won the people's joy—they raised a shrine to him beside the canal.

sentences.zh: 地宜牧，因畜羊三千頭，歲以蕃息，用給貧民無告者。

translations.literal: The land was suited to herding; he therefore kept three thousand sheep, which each year multiplied, and used them to supply poor people with no one to plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: The region was suited to grazing, so he kept three thousand sheep; their annual increase he used to support the destitute.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢河陝汝道，擒巨盜李復岐等，置諸法。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Heshanru Circuit, captured the great robber Li Fuqi and others, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to the Heshanru circuit and captured the notorious bandit Li Fuqi and his gang, who were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 建陝州書院以課士，文風始振。

translations.literal: He built an academy at Shanzhou to instruct scholars, and literary custom began to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy at Shanzhou to train scholars, and local literary culture began to revive.

sentences.zh: 閿鄉城北濱河，南臨澗水，歲屢圮，議築石壩殺水勢，艱於鑿運，竟得石閿底鎮激湍中，工遂成。

translations.literal: North of Minxiang city it bordered the river and south faced the stream water; each year it repeatedly collapsed; they proposed building a stone dam to reduce the water's force; quarrying and transport were difficult, but in the end stone was obtained at the bottom of Min Gorge to anchor the rushing torrent, and the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: North of Minxiang the city fronted the Yellow River and the southern wall faced a torrent that breached the banks yearly. A stone dam was proposed to break the current; quarrying and transport were hard, but stone was finally secured at the bottom of Min Gorge to anchor the rapids, and the work succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏，淫雨河漲，陝城不沒者數版。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixteenth year incessant rain made the river rise; of Shan city only a few courses of wall were not submerged.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixteenth year heavy rains swelled the river until only a few courses of Shan city's walls stood above the flood.

sentences.zh: 民謂官能捍患，恃以不恐。

translations.literal: The people said officials could ward off calamity and relied on this without fear.
translations.idiomatic: The people believed the officials could hold back disaster and took courage from it.

sentences.zh: 鐵珊复築石堤，四月畢工，身親其役，竟以勞卒。

translations.literal: Tie Shan again built a stone embankment; in the fourth month the work was finished; he personally took part in the labor and in the end died from exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Shan rebuilt the stone embankment, finished the work in the fourth month, labored alongside the workers himself, and died of exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 士民請建專祠，詔賜卹。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners requested a dedicated shrine; by edict condolence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and townspeople petitioned for a private shrine; the throne granted condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 桂中行，字履真，江西臨川人，先世賈貴州，遂佔籍鎮遠。

translations.literal: Gui Zhonghang, styled Lüzhen, was a native of Linchuan in Jiangxi; his forebears traded in Guizhou and therefore registered domicile at Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Zhonghang, courtesy name Lüzhen, was from Linchuan in Jiangxi. His family had traded in Guizhou for generations and registered as natives of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 為諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 咸、同間，積軍功，為知縣安徽，署合肥、蒙城、阜陽。

translations.literal: Between Xianfeng and Tongzhi he accumulated military merit, served as magistrate in Anhui, and acted at Hefei, Mengcheng, and Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns he won military honors, became a magistrate in Anhui, and served in acting charge of Hefei, Mengcheng, and Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓率師徵捻，檄中行察勘蒙城圩寨。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan led troops to campaign against the Nian and ordered Zhonghang to inspect and survey the stockaded villages of Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan marched against the Nian, he ordered Zhonghang to survey the fortified villages of Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 蒙城故捻藪也，中行單騎歷諸圩，曉以利害，擇良幹者為圩長。

translations.literal: Mengcheng was formerly a Nian haunt; Zhonghang alone on horseback made the rounds of the stockades, explained advantages and harms, and chose capable men as stockade chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng had long been a Nian stronghold. Zhonghang rode alone from stockade to stockade, explained the stakes, and appointed capable men as village heads.

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，寇無所掠。

translations.literal: They fortified walls and cleared the countryside, and the bandits had nothing to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: With fortified villages and cleared countryside, the rebels had nothing to loot.

sentences.zh: 禮接耆老賢士，從詢方略。

translations.literal: He received elderly worthies and worthy scholars with courtesy and sought strategies from them.
translations.idiomatic: He treated local elders and scholars with respect and sought their counsel.

sentences.zh: 得通捻奸民簿記之，誅其魁桀數十人，豪猾斂跡。

translations.literal: He obtained ledgers of traitorous commoners in contact with the Nian, executed several tens of their ringleaders, and the powerful and cunning drew in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained ledgers of locals colluding with the Nian, executed dozens of ringleaders, and the local bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，威化大行。

translations.literal: After more than a year, authority and transformation were greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year his authority was firmly established.

sentences.zh: 民陷賊及遠徙者，相率還歸。

translations.literal: People who had fallen to the bandits and those who had moved far away came back in succession.
translations.idiomatic: People who had joined the rebels or fled the region returned in droves.

sentences.zh: 以功晉知府。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 調江蘇，筦揚州正陽釐榷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangsu and managed the Zhengyang transit tax at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangsu to manage the Zhengyang transit tax at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，署徐州，以祖母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as acting magistrate of Xuzhou and left office on account of mourning for his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he acted at Xuzhou but left office to mourn his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣城、建平民教閧，焚毀教堂。

translations.literal: In the third year at Xuancheng and Jianping commoners and missionaries clashed in uproar and burned churches.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year riots between commoners and missionaries at Xuancheng and Jianping destroyed churches.

sentences.zh: 總督沈葆楨強起中行往治，中行謂：「民倡亂當治如律，然民所以亂，由教堂侵其地。

translations.literal: Governor Shen Baozhen forcibly recalled Zhonghang to go and settle it; Zhonghang said: 'When the people incite disorder they should be punished according to law, yet the reason the people are disorderly is that the church encroached on their land.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Shen Baozhen pressed Zhonghang back into service to handle the crisis. Zhonghang said: 'Rioters must be punished by law—but they rioted because the church had seized their land.

sentences.zh: 今當令民償教堂財，而教堂還民地。」

translations.literal: Now the people should be made to compensate the church's property, and the church should return the people's land.'
translations.idiomatic: The people should pay for church property destroyed, and the church should return the land.'

sentences.zh: 持數月，卒如中行議。

translations.literal: After several months it ended as Zhonghang had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: After months of negotiation, the settlement followed Zhonghang's proposal.

sentences.zh: 內艱歸，服闋，檄治皖南墾務。

translations.literal: He returned on account of mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was ordered by dispatch to manage reclamation affairs in southern Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother; when mourning ended he was ordered to oversee land reclamation in southern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖南兵燹後，客民佔墾不輸賦，至是清丈田畝，無問主客。

translations.literal: After the warfare in southern Anhui, sojourning people occupied reclaimed land without paying taxes; now they cleared and measured fields, making no distinction between natives and sojourners.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars in southern Anhui, migrant settlers had opened land without paying taxes. Zhonghang ordered a full land survey without favoring either locals or newcomers.

sentences.zh: 客民噪，捕斬其魁，乃聽命。

translations.literal: The sojourning people clamored; he captured and beheaded their chief, and then they obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the migrants protested, he arrested and executed their leader, and the rest submitted.

sentences.zh: 三歲事竣，增賦鉅萬。

translations.literal: In three years the affair was completed and tax revenue increased by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In three years the work was finished and annual revenue rose by tens of thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 九年，補徐州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he received substantive appointment at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received a permanent appointment at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 值水災，興工賑，修堤埝二百餘裡。

translations.literal: He encountered flood disaster, launched relief works, and repaired dikes and embankments for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck, he launched relief projects and repaired more than two hundred li of dikes.

sentences.zh: 又濬邳州艾山河，築宿遷六塘埝，水患除，民以不飢。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Ai Hill River at Pizhou and built the Liutang embankment at Suqian; water calamities were removed and the people thereby did not go hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Ai Hill River at Pizhou and built the Liutang embankment at Suqian, ending the floods and keeping the people fed.

sentences.zh: 治徐十二年，課農勸士，盜賊衰息。

translations.literal: He governed Xuzhou twelve years, urged agriculture and encouraged scholars, and bandits and thieves declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xuzhou for twelve years, promoted farming and learning, and crime dwindled.

sentences.zh: 擢岳常澧道，數月，遷廣西按察使，復調湖南。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Yuechangli Circuit, and within several months was moved to Guangxi provincial judge and again transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Yuechangli circuit, then within months became provincial judge of Guangxi and was transferred again to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 中行所至有聲，官江南最久，民尤愛戴之。

translations.literal: Wherever Zhonghang went he had a reputation; he served longest in Jiangnan, and the people especially loved and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghang won renown wherever he served; he spent the longest time in Jiangnan, where the people loved him most.

sentences.zh: 附祀徐州曾國籓祠。

translations.literal: He was attached for worship in Zeng Guofan's shrine at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a place in Zeng Guofan's shrine at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉含芳，字薌林，安徽貴池人。

translations.literal: Liu Hanfang, styled Xianglin, was a native of Guichi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanfang, courtesy name Xianglin, was from Guichi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治初，李鴻章率師東征，從克蘇州，司運糧械。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi Li Hongzhang led troops east in campaign; he followed in taking Suzhou and managed transport of grain and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he joined Li Hongzhang's eastern campaign, helped take Suzhou, and managed supply transport.

sentences.zh: 後隨徵捻，積功至道員。

translations.literal: Later he followed in campaigning against the Nian, accumulated merit to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against the Nian and rose to circuit intendant by merit.

sentences.zh: 鴻章督直隸，命含芳治軍械天津。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang governed Zhili he ordered Hanfang to manage military stores at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang became governor-general of Zhili, he put Hanfang in charge of ordnance at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 得西洋利器，省覽機括，久之悉通其意。

translations.literal: He obtained Western weapons, examined their mechanisms, and after a long time fully understood their principles.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Western arms, examined their mechanisms, and in time mastered how they worked.

sentences.zh: 鴻章方拓北洋軍備，於西沽建武庫，廣收博儲，以肄將士，擴充機器、製造兩局，募工仿構，創設電氣水雷學堂，編立水雷營，皆以含芳董其役。

translations.literal: Hongzhang was then expanding Beiyang military preparations; at Xigu he built an arsenal, broadly collected and stored, to drill officers and soldiers; he expanded the Machinery and Manufacturing bureaus, recruited workers to imitate construction, established an electrical torpedo school, and organized torpedo battalions—all with Hanfang directing the tasks.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Hongzhang built up Beiyang defenses, Hanfang directed his projects: the arsenal at Xigu, expanded Machinery and Manufacturing bureaus, workshops copying Western designs, a naval torpedo school, and torpedo battalions.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，詔求人才，以鴻章薦，交軍機處存記。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu an edict sought talented men; on Hongzhang's recommendation he was referred to the Grand Council for record.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Guangxu the throne called for talent; on Li Hongzhang's recommendation Hanfang was registered with the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 時海軍初立，造船塢旅順，含芳兼領沿海水陸營務處。

translations.literal: At the time the navy was newly established and the shipyard was at Lüshun; Hanfang concurrently headed the coastal land and water camp affairs office.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy was first formed and the dockyard built at Lüshun, Hanfang also headed the coastal defense office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，署津海關道，授甘肅安肅道，留治海防。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served as acting Jinghai customs circuit intendant, was appointed Gansu Ansu Circuit intendant, but was retained to manage coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he acted as Jinghai customs intendant and was appointed to Gansu Ansu Circuit but was kept at his coastal-defense duties.

sentences.zh: 尋調山東登萊青道，監督東海關，十九年，始之任。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Shandong Denglaiqing Circuit, supervised the East Sea Customs, and in the nineteenth year first went to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Denglaiqing circuit in Shandong to supervise the East Sea Customs, taking up the post in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 含芳自隨鴻章至天津，凡十四載，屯旅順十一載，至是雖領一道，猶隸於北洋。

translations.literal: Hanfang had followed Hongzhang to Tianjin for fourteen years in all and was stationed at Lüshun eleven years; even now though he held a circuit post he still belonged under Beiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanfang had followed Li Hongzhang to Tianjin for fourteen years and spent eleven at Lüshun; even as a circuit intendant he remained under Beiyang command.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遼東兵事起，海陸軍屢挫，旅順、威海相繼陷。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year military affairs began in Liaodong; land and sea forces were repeatedly defeated, and Lüshun and Weihai fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year war broke out in Liaodong. Land and sea forces suffered repeated defeats, and Lüshun and Weihai fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 登萊青道駐煙台，敵軍日逼。

translations.literal: The Denglaiqing circuit office was stationed at Yantai, and the enemy army pressed daily closer.
translations.idiomatic: The Denglaiqing intendant was based at Yantai as the enemy drew nearer day by day.

sentences.zh: 俄報軍艦沒於劉公島，寧海亦陷，敵前鋒距煙台十餘裡。

translations.literal: Soon came report that warships were lost at Liugong Island, Ninghai also fell, and the enemy vanguard was a dozen-odd li from Yantai.
translations.idiomatic: News came that the fleet was destroyed at Liugong Island and Ninghai had fallen; enemy vanguards were barely a dozen li from Yantai.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫李秉衡亦駐師煙台。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Li Bingheng also stationed troops at Yantai.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Bingheng had also stationed troops at Yantai.

sentences.zh: 西國諸領事言巡撫在，則敵攻之急，於租地不便，巡撫乃退萊州。

translations.literal: Western consuls said that if the governor were present the enemy would attack urgently, which would be inconvenient for the leased territories; the governor then withdrew to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Western consuls said that with the governor present the enemy would press the attack and endanger the treaty ports, so Li withdrew to Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 領事復言含芳，含芳曰：「巡撫大臣也，可去。

translations.literal: The consuls again spoke of Hanfang; Hanfang said: 'The governor is a great minister and may leave.
translations.idiomatic: The consuls then spoke to Hanfang. He replied: 'The governor is a high minister and may leave.

sentences.zh: 某守土吏，去何之？

translations.literal: I am an official who guards the soil—where would I go?
translations.idiomatic: I am the local magistrate—where would I go?

sentences.zh: 今死此矣！」

translations.literal: Now I die here!'
translations.idiomatic: I will die here!'

sentences.zh: 因置鴆二盂案上，與其妻郝冠服坐待，意氣堅定，民恃無恐。

translations.literal: He therefore placed two cups of poison on the table, and with his wife Hao in full dress they sat waiting; his spirit was firm, and the people relied on this without fear.
translations.idiomatic: He set out two cups of poison on his desk, and he and his wife Hao sat in full dress waiting. His resolve steadied the people.

sentences.zh: 有潰卒數千，持兵噪呼求食。

translations.literal: There were several thousand routed soldiers who held weapons, clamored, and demanded food.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand routed soldiers appeared, armed and clamoring for food.

sentences.zh: 含芳單騎馳諭，處以空營，重為編伍，不原留者厚給遣之，皆出私財。

translations.literal: Hanfang alone on horseback galloped to instruct them, quartered them in empty camps, reorganized them into units, and those unwilling to stay he generously paid to dismiss—all from private wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Hanfang rode out alone to address them, quartered them in empty barracks, reorganized the ranks, and paid those who would not stay to leave—all from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 初，西人聞潰兵，甚戒嚴，俄而散遣，殊出不意，咸稱道之。

translations.literal: At first Westerners hearing of routed troops were very much on alert; soon they were dispersed and dismissed, quite beyond expectation, and all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners had been alarmed at news of the routed troops; when they were quietly dispersed, all praised Hanfang's handling.

sentences.zh: 和議成，奏派渡海勘收還地。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he memorialized to be assigned to cross the sea and survey the recovery of returned territory.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was signed he was ordered to cross the sea and survey the recovered territories.

sentences.zh: 始威海、旅順、大連灣皆荒島，含芳瘁心力營構十餘年，所成險塞，至是見盡毀矣，因憤慨流涕，以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: At first Weihai, Lüshun, and Dalian Bay were all barren islands; Hanfang exhausted mind and strength building for more than ten years—the strongholds he had made were now seen utterly destroyed; he therefore indignantly shed tears and begged leave to return home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Weihai, Lüshun, and Dalian Bay had once been barren islands; Hanfang had spent more than a decade building their defenses, now utterly destroyed. He wept in grief and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 陳黌舉，字序賓，安徽石埭人。

translations.literal: Chen Hongju, styled Xubin, was a native of Shidi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hongju, courtesy name Xubin, was from Shidi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少從其鄉陳艾遊，以諸生為曾國籓所識拔。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his townsman Chen Ai in study; as a licentiate he was recognized and promoted by Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under his townsman Chen Ai; as a licentiate he won Zeng Guofan's notice and patronage.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章督師，令主辦行營支應。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang commanded the army he ordered him to take charge of field headquarters supply.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang took command, he put Hongju in charge of field headquarters logistics.

sentences.zh: 或謂「大軍轉餉關天下，往者輒命大臣，今以諸生任耶」？

translations.literal: Some said, 'The great army's transport of pay concerns the realm; in the past great ministers were always appointed—now a licentiate is to be entrusted?'
translations.idiomatic: Some objected: 'Army supply concerns the whole empire—past appointees were great ministers. You would entrust this to a mere licentiate?'

sentences.zh: 卒用不疑。

translations.literal: In the end he was employed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Li used him anyway, without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 自粵亂作，海內困軍餉。

translations.literal: Since the Guangdong rebellion arose, the realm was strained by military pay.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taiping rebellion, the empire had been crushed under the burden of military pay.

sentences.zh: 黌舉曰：「餉糜則斂重，戰久則餉虧，兵不潰，民且寇矣。」

translations.literal: Hongju said: 'When pay is wasted then levies grow heavy; when war lasts long then pay runs short; if the troops do not mutiny, the people will become bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongju said: 'Waste in pay means heavier taxes; long war means empty coffers. If the army does not mutiny, the people will rise as rebels.'

sentences.zh: 乃釐訂條款，杜絕冒濫。

translations.literal: He therefore drew up regulations and cut off false claims and excess.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up strict regulations and stamped out fraud.

sentences.zh: 軍行數載，餉節民和，平捻之功實基此。

translations.literal: The army marched several years; pay was economized and the people were harmonious; the achievement of pacifying the Nian in truth rested on this.
translations.idiomatic: For years the armies marched with controlled pay and contented civilians—the foundation of victory over the Nian lay here.

sentences.zh: 鴻章移直隸籌海防，凡砲台、船塢、製造、電報及疏河、屯田諸役，需費尤鉅，皆倚之以辦。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang moved to Zhili to plan coastal defense, all batteries, dockyards, manufacturing, telegraph, river dredging, and garrison farming projects needing especially great expense all relied on him to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: When Li moved to Zhili to build coastal defenses, Hongju managed the vast expenses of batteries, dockyards, factories, telegraph lines, river works, and garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 先後綜軍糈二十餘年，一介不苟。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years in all he oversaw army provisions and accepted not a single improper gift.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years he managed army funds without taking a single improper gift.

sentences.zh: 將吏服其廉潔，雖被裁抑，無怨言。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks submitted to his integrity; even when cut in pay they had no complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Officers respected his integrity; even when he cut their allowances, they did not complain.

sentences.zh: 直、晉大災，兼籌賑務，廢寢忘食，稽核勤摯，人不忍欺。

translations.literal: Great disasters struck Zhili and Shanxi; he also planned relief affairs, forgot sleep and food, examined accounts diligently and sincerely, and people could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: During great famines in Zhili and Shanxi he also ran relief work, working day and night with meticulous audits that no one dared cheat.

sentences.zh: 以私款歸實濟，全活以億萬計，眾皆德之。

translations.literal: He used private funds for real benefit; those preserved alive numbered in the hundreds of millions, and all were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He spent private funds on real relief and saved countless lives; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 旋以積勞病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness from accumulated labor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness brought on by overwork.

sentences.zh: 初由訓導累功至知府，詔贈道員。

translations.literal: At first from instructor he accumulated merit to prefect; by edict he was posthumously given circuit intendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen from instructor to prefect by merit; the throne posthumously granted him circuit intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 與含芳同附祀鴻章祠，入祀淮軍昭忠祠，並祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Together with Hanfang he was attached for worship in Hongzhang's shrine, entered worship in the Huai Army Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, and was also worshipped among local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored alongside Hanfang in Li Hongzhang's shrine, the Huai Army martyrs' shrine, and the local worthies' temple.

sentences.zh: 黌舉子惟彥，亦見重於鴻章，命繼司軍計。

translations.literal: Hongju's son Wei Yan was also esteemed by Hongzhang, who ordered him to succeed in managing military accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Hongju's son Wei Yan also won Li Hongzhang's trust and succeeded his father as army paymaster.

sentences.zh: 由大理寺丞累保知府，官貴州，歷開州、婺川，調守黎平。

translations.literal: From vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review he was repeatedly recommended to prefect, served in Guizhou, passed through Kaizhou and Wuchuan, and was transferred to guard Liping.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review to prefect by repeated recommendation, he served in Guizhou at Kaizhou and Wuchuan before transferring to Liping.

sentences.zh: 首革票差催糧，遏龍世渭逆謀，破鴨販彭三等血案，遠近驚為神明。

translations.literal: He first abolished ticket runners pressing for grain tax, checked Long Shiwei's treasonous plot, broke the bloody cases of duck peddlers Peng San and others, and far and near were astonished, calling him a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished corrupt tax runners, foiled Long Shiwei's conspiracy, solved the notorious duck-peddler murders, and won awe throughout the region as a judge of uncanny insight.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有訟，往往越境就訴。

translations.literal: When neighboring districts had lawsuits, people often crossed borders to bring suit before him.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants from neighboring counties often crossed borders to bring cases before him.

sentences.zh: 興學育才，並創立體仁堂養老恤孤，勸工習藝，政聲頗著。

translations.literal: He promoted schools and nurtured talent, and also founded the Tiren Hall to support the aged and succor orphans, urged labor and training in crafts, and his governmental reputation was quite outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted schools, founded the Tiren Hall for the aged and orphans, encouraged trades training, and won a strong reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 巡撫疏為良吏第一，以道員改江蘇，總釐捐，任督銷。

translations.literal: The governor memorialized him as the foremost good official, changed him to Jiangsu as circuit intendant, oversaw transit levies, and charged him with supervising sales.
translations.idiomatic: The governor ranked him the finest official in the province; he was transferred to Jiangsu as circuit intendant to oversee transit levies and sales.

sentences.zh: 去弊化私，以廉直稱。

translations.literal: He removed abuses and transformed private interests, and was known for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out corruption and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 旋授湖南財政監理官，复委辦兩淮鹽政，創設淮南公所，歲增至二百萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hunan fiscal supervisor, again was entrusted with managing Lianghuai salt affairs, established the Huainan public office, and annual revenue increased to two million.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Hunan fiscal supervisor, then entrusted with Lianghuai salt administration; he founded the Huainan office and raised annual revenue to two million taels.

sentences.zh: 歸，與弟惟壬於縣境修巨橋跨舒溪，亙六十餘丈，便行旅。

translations.literal: Returning home, with his younger brother Wei Ren he built a great bridge spanning the Shu Stream in the county territory, extending more than sixty zhang, convenient for travelers.
translations.idiomatic: At home he and his brother Wei Ren built a great bridge more than sixty zhang long across the Shu Stream for travelers.

sentences.zh: 邑人私諡曰慈惠。

translations.literal: The townspeople privately gave him the posthumous title Kind and Beneficent.
translations.idiomatic: Locals gave him the private posthumous title Kind and Beneficent.

translations.literal: Note one.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial marker for note one following.

sentences.zh: 遊智開，字子代，湖南新化人。

translations.literal: You Zhikai, styled Zidai, was a native of Xinhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhikai, courtesy name Zidai, was from Xinhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年舉人，揀選知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he became a provincial graduate and was selected as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of the first year of Xianfeng, he was selected for magistrate rank.

sentences.zh: 同治初，李續宜巡撫安徽，調司釐榷，以廉平稱。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi Li Xuyi was governor of Anhui and transferred him to manage transit levies; he was known for integrity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, when Li Xuyi governed Anhui, Zhikai was put in charge of transit levies and won a name for fairness.

sentences.zh: 四年，署和州知州，日坐堂皇決事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served as acting prefect of Hezhou and daily sat in the main hall to decide cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he acted as prefect of Hezhou and heard cases daily in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 又時出巡四境，延見父老，問其疾苦。

translations.literal: He also from time to time went out to tour the four quarters, received elderly men, and asked their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the countryside, met elders, and asked about their hardships.

sentences.zh: 親為諸生考校文藝，剖析經旨，教以孝弟廉讓。

translations.literal: He personally examined students in literary arts, analyzed the meaning of the classics, and taught filial piety, brotherly respect, integrity, and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He personally examined students' essays, explained the classics, and taught filial piety, integrity, and humility.

sentences.zh: 期年，治化大行。

translations.literal: Within a year, governance and transformation were greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year good government took hold.

sentences.zh: 州舊由胥吏墊完糧賦，最為民病，禁絕之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had formerly had clerks advance grain tax payments, which most harmed the people; he forbade this entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks had long advanced tax payments at the people's expense; he banned the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 築瀕江堤防，自督工役，費節而堤堅，免水患。

translations.literal: He built riverfront dikes, personally supervised the labor, economized expenses while the dikes were solid, and avoided flood calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He built river dikes under his own supervision, kept costs low while making them strong, and ended flooding.

sentences.zh: 補無為州，署泗州，治盜尤嚴。

translations.literal: He received substantive appointment at Wuwei Prefecture, served as acting at Sizhou, and governed bandits with especial severity.
translations.idiomatic: He took permanent office at Wuwei, acted at Sizhou, and was especially severe on banditry.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓稱其治行為江南第一，移督直隸，調智開署深州。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan called his record of governance the first in Jiangnan; when he moved to govern Zhili he transferred Zhikai to act at Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan called his administration the best in Jiangnan; when Zeng moved to Zhili he transferred Zhikai to act at Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 興義學，減浮徵，民大悅。

translations.literal: He promoted righteous learning and reduced excessive levies; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted schools and cut excessive levies; the people were delighted.

sentences.zh: 補灤州，民苦兵車，為別籌輸送，免擾累。

translations.literal: He received substantive appointment at Luanzhou; the people suffered from military transport; he separately planned delivery and spared them harassment and burden.
translations.idiomatic: At Luanzhou, where the people suffered from military transport, he arranged separate supply routes to spare them the burden.

sentences.zh: 俗健訟，奸民居間交構，痛懲之，其風漸息。

translations.literal: The custom was fond of litigation; wicked people lived among them stirring strife; he punished severely and the custom gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Litigation was rampant and troublemakers stirred disputes; he punished them severely until the practice faded.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢知永平府，一車一蓋，週曆下邑，得其情偽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to prefect of Yongping, with one cart and one canopy, made a circuit of subordinate districts, and learned the true and false of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became prefect of Yongping. With only a cart and umbrella he toured every subordinate district and learned the truth on the ground.

sentences.zh: 遇有事，牧令未及報，輒已聞知。

translations.literal: When something occurred, before district magistrates had reported he already knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arose, he often knew of it before his subordinates could report.

sentences.zh: 一日侵晨，馳至遷安獄，獄吏方私系囚求賂，即拘吏至縣庭笞之。

translations.literal: One day at dawn he galloped to the Qian'an jail; the jailer was privately detaining a prisoner to seek a bribe; he immediately seized the clerk and brought him to the county court for beating.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn he rode to the Qian'an jail and caught a jailer extorting a prisoner; he had the man flogged in the county court at once.

sentences.zh: 令始驚，起謝。

translations.literal: The magistrate was only then startled and rose to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate, startled awake, rose to thank him.

sentences.zh: 葺書院，築城垣，修郡志，皆事舉，無濫費。

translations.literal: He repaired the academy, built city walls, and revised the prefectural gazetteer; all affairs were accomplished without wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the academy, rebuilt the walls, and revised the prefectural gazetteer—all completed without waste.

sentences.zh: 瀕海產鹽，貧民資為衣食。

translations.literal: Along the coast salt was produced; poor people relied on it for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal salt production was how the poor made their living.

sentences.zh: 部牒禁私販，疏官引。

translations.literal: The ministry dispatched orders forbidding private sale and proposed official salt tickets.
