translations.idiomatic: The ministry ordered an end to private salt sales and proposed official salt tickets.

sentences.zh: 智開上言民間少一私販，即地方多一馬賊。

translations.literal: Zhikai memorialized that for the common people, one fewer private salt seller meant one more horse bandit in the locality.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikai memorialized: every private salt seller driven out of business becomes a bandit.

sentences.zh: 鹽本宜行官引，惟永平則仍舊為便，事得寢。

translations.literal: Salt in general ought to use official tickets, but only at Yongping the old ways were still convenient; the matter was allowed to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Official tickets might suit elsewhere, but Yongping was better left as before; the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 有巨室以析產構訟，久不決。

translations.literal: A great family sued over division of property; it long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy family's inheritance dispute had dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 智開坐便室，呼兩造至，不加研鞫，自咎治郡無狀，變起骨肉，望族如此，況齊民乎？

translations.literal: Zhikai sat in a side room, summoned both parties, added no interrogation, blamed himself that governing the prefecture had been without merit, that trouble arose among kin, and if eminent clans were thus, how much more common people?
translations.idiomatic: Zhikai called both sides to a side room without interrogation and blamed himself: 'My rule has failed if even eminent families feud like this—what of ordinary people?'

sentences.zh: 訟者流涕請罷。

translations.literal: The litigants wept and asked to withdraw the suit.
translations.idiomatic: The litigants wept and asked to drop the case.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏陳智開清勤端嚴，足勵末俗。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized that Zhikai was pure, diligent, upright, and strict, sufficient to encourage declining customs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized that Zhikai's integrity and severity could revive declining morals.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，擢永定河道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was promoted to commissioner of the Yongding River course.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was named commissioner of the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 河患夙稱難治，智開每當搶護險工，立河乾親指揮，日週巡兩岸以為常，員弁無敢離工次者。

translations.literal: River calamities had long been called hard to govern; whenever Zhikai rushed to protect dangerous works he stood on the dry riverbed personally directing; daily circuit of both banks was his custom, and officers dared not leave their work posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongding had a reputation as ungovernable. At every emergency Zhikai stood on the dry riverbed directing repairs himself, patrolled both banks daily, and allowed no officer to leave his post.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠議將永定河南岸改北岸以紓水患。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang proposed shifting the Yongding River's south bank to the north bank to ease flood calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang proposed moving the south bank works to the north bank to ease flooding.

sentences.zh: 智開以上下游數百里，城市廬墓，遷徙不便，力爭而止。

translations.literal: Zhikai argued that for several hundred li up and down stream were cities, houses, and tombs, relocation would be inconvenient, and he strove against it until it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikai argued that cities, homes, and tombs lined hundreds of li of river and relocation was impossible; he fought the plan until it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 兩以三汛安瀾邀優獎。

translations.literal: Twice for three flood seasons of peaceful waters he received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he won special rewards for three consecutive flood seasons without breach.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢四川按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Sichuan provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to provincial judge of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 攜一僕乘箯輿入蜀，密訪吏治得失，民情愛惡。

translations.literal: Carrying one servant he entered Shu in a bamboo sedan, secretly inquired into the gains and losses of official governance and the people's loves and hates.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Sichuan with a single servant in a bamboo sedan, quietly investigating official performance and public sentiment.

sentences.zh: 督屬清釐積案，常躬自訊結，獄訟為清。

translations.literal: He urged subordinates to clear accumulated cases, often personally examined and concluded them, and lawsuits were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered subordinates to clear backlogged cases and often heard them himself until the courts were clear.

sentences.zh: 兩權布政使。

translations.literal: Twice he held acting provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He twice acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十二年，護理總督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 重慶教案起，智開奏言是案當以根究起釁之由，先收險要及預定款目為關鍵。

translations.literal: The Chongqing church case arose; Zhikai memorialized that this case ought to take tracing the cause of provocation as root, and first securing strategic points and predetermined payment items as the key.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongqing missionary case broke out, Zhikai argued that the key was to establish who provoked it, secure strategic points, and settle terms in advance.

sentences.zh: 非贖回險要，無以服渝民之心；

translations.literal: Without recovering strategic points there was no way to satisfy the hearts of Chongqing people;
translations.idiomatic: Without recovering strategic points, Chongqing's people would never be satisfied;

sentences.zh: 非嚴誅首犯，無以製洋人之口；

translations.literal: without severely punishing the chief offenders there was no way to restrain the foreigners' mouths;
translations.idiomatic: without punishing the ringleaders, foreigners would never be silenced;

sentences.zh: 非議賠銀兩，無以為結案之具。

translations.literal: without negotiating indemnity in silver there was no means to conclude the case.
translations.idiomatic: without agreeing on indemnity, there was no way to close the case.

sentences.zh: 諗知教首羅元義激成眾怒，幾釀大變，飛檄拘之入省，民團始散。

translations.literal: Learning that church leader Luo Yuanyi had provoked popular anger and nearly brewed a great upheaval, he sent urgent dispatches to seize him into the province, and the people's militia then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that church leader Luo Yuanyi had provoked the mob and nearly caused a catastrophe, he ordered him seized and brought to the provincial capital; only then did the militia disperse.

sentences.zh: 又以元義身雖入教，仍是中國子民，自應治以中國法律。

translations.literal: He further argued that though Yuanyi had entered the church, he was still a subject of China and ought naturally to be punished by Chinese law.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that though Luo had joined the church, he remained a Chinese subject and must be tried under Chinese law.

sentences.zh: 請敕總理衙門據理與爭，勿許公使乾預。

translations.literal: He requested that the Zongli Yamen be ordered to contend according to reason and not permit the minister to interfere.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Zongli Yamen to argue on principle and refuse ministerial interference.

sentences.zh: 時中外皆恐以肇釁端，智開持之益力，卒置元義於法。

translations.literal: At the time Chinese and foreigners alike feared this would provoke an incident; Zhikai held all the firmer and in the end punished Yuanyi according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Both Chinese and foreigners feared war, but Zhikai held firm and executed Luo under Chinese law.

sentences.zh: 薄給賠償，而案遂結。

translations.literal: A small indemnity was given, and the case was then concluded.
translations.idiomatic: A modest indemnity was paid and the case closed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷廣東布政使，署理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Guangdong provincial treasurer and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became provincial treasurer of Guangdong and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 劾貪墨吏，不避權要，嚴賭禁，卻闈姓例餽三十萬金。

translations.literal: He impeached corrupt officials without avoiding the powerful, strictly forbade gambling, and refused the customary thirty thousand taels of gold from examination patrons.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached corrupt officials regardless of rank, banned gambling, and refused three hundred thousand taels in customary examination bribes.

sentences.zh: 僧寺匿匪，廢改義塾。

translations.literal: Buddhist temples harbored bandits; he abolished them and converted them to charity schools.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries hiding bandits were closed and turned into charity schools.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以老乞休。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, on account of age he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as Guangxi provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as provincial treasurer of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 為政務持大體，事有不可行，力持不變。

translations.literal: In governing he grasped the great principles; when something could not be done he firmly held without change.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by broad principles and stood firm when he believed a policy was wrong.

sentences.zh: 痛除官場積習，僚屬化之。

translations.literal: He bitterly eradicated long-standing habits of officialdom, and colleagues were transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out entrenched official corruption, and his subordinates followed his example.

sentences.zh: 靈川鬧糧，省令發兵剿辦。

translations.literal: At Lingchuan there was a grain-tax riot; the province ordered troops sent to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingchuan erupted over grain taxes, the province ordered troops to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 智開以事由激變，辦理不善，責歸縣令，民獲保全。

translations.literal: Zhikai held that the affair arose from provocation and poor handling, placed blame on the county magistrate, and the people were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikai held that provocation and poor county administration had caused the riot; he blamed the magistrate and spared the people.

sentences.zh: 又念粵西地瘠，向鮮蓋藏，捐廉儲糧石，通飭各屬積穀備荒。

translations.literal: He also reflected that western Guangdong land was poor and had always had little stored grain; he donated from his salary to store grain and broadly ordered all jurisdictions to accumulate grain against famine.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing western Guangxi was poor and rarely had reserves, he donated salary grain and ordered every district to build famine stores.

sentences.zh: 凡廉俸所入，悉以辦公益，無自私。

translations.literal: All income from his salary he used entirely for public benefit, with nothing private.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire salary on public works and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 閱三年，因病罷歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: After three years he was dismissed and returned home on account of illness, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he went home ill and died there.

sentences.zh: 所至各省俱請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: In every province where he went, all requested his worship in the shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Every province where he served petitioned for his entry in the shrine of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 李用清，字澄齋，山西平定州人。

translations.literal: Li Yongqing, styled Chengzhai, was a native of Pingding Prefecture in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yongqing, courtesy name Chengzhai, was from Pingding in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 同治四年進士，改庶吉士，出大學士倭仁門，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, came from the school of Grand Secretary Woren, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Tongzhi, he became a Hanlin bachelor under Grand Secretary Woren and later a compiler.

sentences.zh: 安貧厲節，日研四子書、硃子小學，旁稽掌故，於物力豐瘠，尤所留意。

translations.literal: Content in poverty and strict in integrity, daily he studied the Four Books and Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning, consulted records on the side, and especially attended to the abundance or scarcity of material resources.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but principled, he studied the Four Books and Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning daily, consulted historical records, and paid special attention to economic conditions.

sentences.zh: 大婚禮成，加侍讀銜。

translations.literal: When the Grand Wedding was completed he was given the rank of attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Wedding ceremonies he received the attendant reader rank.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丁父憂，徒步扶櫬返葬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he mourned his father, walked on foot supporting the coffin, and returned to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, mourning his father, he walked home on foot escorting the coffin.

sentences.zh: 服闋，入都，仍課生徒自給。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered the capital and still taught students to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned to the capital and supported himself by teaching students.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，記名御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was registered by name as censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was placed on the censorial register.

sentences.zh: 會山西奇荒，巡撫曾國荃、欽差大臣閻敬銘奏調用清襄賑務，騎一驢週曆全境，無間寒暑，一僕荷裝從。

translations.literal: Coinciding with Shanxi's extraordinary famine, Governor Zeng Guoquan and Imperial Commissioner Yan Jingming memorialized to transfer Yongqing to aid relief affairs; he rode one donkey and made a circuit of the entire territory without regard to cold or heat, one servant carrying gear following.
translations.idiomatic: During Shanxi's terrible famine, Governors Zeng Guoquan and Yan Jingming called him to help with relief. He toured the entire province on a donkey in all seasons, with one servant carrying his baggage.

sentences.zh: 凡災情輕重、食糧轉輸要道，悉紀之冊。

translations.literal: All degrees of disaster severity and key routes for food transport he fully recorded in registers.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded every degree of disaster and every critical grain route in his notebooks.

sentences.zh: 深窮病源，以為晉省罌粟花田彌望無際，必改花田而種五穀，然後生聚有期，元氣可復，上書國荃詳論之。

translations.literal: He deeply investigated the roots of the disease and held that in Shanxi Province poppy fields stretched boundlessly; they must change flower fields and plant the five grains, and only then would population growth have a term and vital energy could recover; he wrote to Guoquan discussing this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Probing the roots of the crisis, he concluded that Shanxi's endless poppy fields must be converted to grain before the province could recover; he wrote a detailed memorial to Zeng Guoquan.

sentences.zh: 國荃疑晉新荒，禁煙效緩，且全國未禁，徙斂怨，說竟不行。

translations.literal: Guoquan doubted that Shanxi was newly devastated, that prohibiting opium would be slow in effect, and that the whole country was not yet prohibited—only stirring resentment; the proposal in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng doubted that a ban would work in a province just devastated by famine, or before a national prohibition—and feared it would only breed resentment. The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 賑竣，卻保獎。

translations.literal: When relief was finished he declined recommendation for reward.
translations.idiomatic: When relief ended he declined recommendations for reward.

sentences.zh: 還京，傳補御史，引見有日矣。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was transmitted for appointment as censor and audience was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he was slated for censorial appointment and imminent audience with the throne.

sentences.zh: 法越事萌芽，張樹聲以廣西邊防奏調。

translations.literal: The Franco-Vietnamese affair was sprouting; Zhang Shusheng memorialized to transfer him for Guangxi border defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the Sino-French conflict began, Zhang Shusheng called him to Guangxi border defense.

sentences.zh: 樹聲督兩廣，復調廣東任海防釐榷，洗手奉職。

translations.literal: Shusheng governed Liangguang and again transferred him to Guangdong to hold coastal defense transit levies, serving with clean hands and devoted duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang governed Liangguang he transferred Yongqing to Guangdong coastal defense levies, where he served with scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 七年，授惠州知府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the reign he was appointed prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 境故多盜，喜博，喜私鬥。

translations.literal: The jurisdiction had long had many bandits; the people loved gambling and loved private brawling.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long been plagued by bandits, gambling, and private feuds.

sentences.zh: 用清推誠化之，俗乃稍革。

translations.literal: Yongqing with sincerity and trust reformed them, and customs then slightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing won them over with frank sincerity, and local customs gradually improved.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷貴州貴西道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Guixi Circuit of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Guixi Circuit in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，超擢布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: The next year he was exceptionally promoted to provincial treasurer and served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted ahead of schedule to provincial treasurer and acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 實倉儲，興農利，裁冗員，劾缺額之提鎮，擒粵匪莫夢弼等置諸法。

translations.literal: He filled granaries, promoted agricultural profit, cut redundant posts, impeached brigade generals below quota, and captured the Guangdong bandit Mo Mengbi and others and subjected them to the law.
translations.idiomatic: He filled the granaries, promoted agriculture, cut redundant posts, impeached brigade commanders who fell short of their quotas, and captured the Guangdong rebel Mo Mengbi and others, bringing them to justice.

sentences.zh: 巡閱所至，召士子講說經傳，將吏環聽，相與動容。

translations.literal: Wherever his inspection tours took him, he summoned scholars to lecture on the classics; officers and officials surrounded him listening, and all were moved together.
translations.idiomatic: On his inspection tours he summoned local scholars to lecture on the classics; military and civil officials gathered round to listen, and all were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 黔地土瘠，多種罌粟，暢行湘、鄂、贛、粵諸省，用清奏陳禁種之法，分區限年，時自出巡，刈剷菸苗。

translations.literal: Guizhou's land was barren and poppies were widely planted; the drug flowed freely through Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Guangdong. Yongqing memorialized methods to prohibit planting, divided zones and set year limits, and from time to time went out on tour himself to cut down and uproot opium seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou's soil was poor and poppy cultivation was widespread; the opium trade reached freely into Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Guangdong. Yongqing memorialized a prohibition scheme with zoned deadlines, and often toured in person to cut down poppy crops.

sentences.zh: 言者疑其操之過急。

translations.literal: Critics suspected his handling was too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Some critics thought he was pushing the policy too hard.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，有旨來京候簡。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year an imperial order came for him to proceed to the capital and await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eleventh year he was ordered to the capital to await a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 召對，猶痛陳罌粟疚國殃民狀，冀可挽回萬一。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he still bitterly set forth how poppies harmed the state and brought calamity on the people, hoping perhaps to turn back the tide even one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he still spoke passionately of how opium was ruining the country and destroying the people, hoping against hope to change policy.

sentences.zh: 旋命署陝西布政使，荒燹之後，休養生息，仍嚴煙禁。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to serve as acting provincial treasurer of Shaanxi; after devastation by famine and war he nurtured recovery and rest, and still strictly enforced the opium ban.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting provincial treasurer of Shaanxi. In a province ravaged by famine and war he worked to restore prosperity, while keeping the opium prohibition strictly in force.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復命來京候簡，遂以疾歸，主講晉陽書院凡十年。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again ordered to come to the capital and await appointment; then, owing to illness, he returned home and lectured at Jinyang Academy for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was again summoned to the capital for appointment, but illness forced him home, where he taught at Jinyang Academy for ten years.

sentences.zh: 用清嚴於自治，勇於奉公。

translations.literal: Yongqing was strict in governing himself and bold in serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing was austere in his private life and fearless in public service.

sentences.zh: 籓黔時，庫儲六萬，年餘存十六萬，陝庫三十萬，再期六十餘萬矣。

translations.literal: When he governed Guizhou the treasury held sixty thousand taels; after a little more than a year one hundred sixty thousand remained. The Shaanxi treasury held thirty thousand, and in two terms of office more than six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Guizhou the treasury held sixty thousand taels; within a year he had built it to one hundred sixty thousand. In Shaanxi he inherited thirty thousand and left more than six hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 所至尤措意桑棉織組。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he especially attended to mulberry, cotton, weaving, and embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he gave special attention to sericulture, cotton, weaving, and textile crafts.

sentences.zh: 嘗濬三源縣龍渠，溉田千餘畝。

translations.literal: Once he dredged the Long Canal in Sanyuan County and irrigated more than a thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He once dredged the Long Canal in Sanyuan County, irrigating more than a thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 俸入不以自潤，於黔以購粟六千石，於陝購萬石，備不虞。

translations.literal: He did not use his salary income to enrich himself; in Guizhou he purchased six thousand shi of grain, and in Shaanxi ten thousand shi, to prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He never spent his salary on himself. In Guizhou he bought six thousand shi of grain; in Shaanxi, ten thousand—stores against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 鄭州河決，捐工需二萬兩。

translations.literal: When the Zhengzhou river broke its banks, labor relief required a donation of twenty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengzhou river burst its banks he donated twenty thousand taels toward labor relief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fourth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子貴陽扶柩歸，以毀殤。

translations.literal: His son Guiyang escorted the coffin home and died from grief at the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guiyang escorted the coffin home and died of grief in mourning.

sentences.zh: 同縣李希蓮，字亦青。

translations.literal: A townsman of the same county, Li Xilian, styled Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman, Li Xilian, whose courtesy name was Yiqing,

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士，授戶部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Xianfeng, he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and was twice promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Xianfeng and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, later rising twice to the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 性節儉，官京曹三十年，車馬羸敝，不顧訕譏。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal; he served in the capital ministries for thirty years with worn-out carriage and horses, heedless of ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he spent thirty years in the capital ministries with a shabby carriage and broken-down horses, indifferent to mockery.

sentences.zh: 英、法兵入都，曹司多走避，希蓮昕夕詣署無間。

translations.literal: When British and French troops entered the capital, many ministry officials fled; Xilian morning and evening went to his office without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: When British and French troops entered the capital, most ministry officials fled—but Xilian reported to his office morning and night without fail.

sentences.zh: 以忤肅順，乞假歸。

translations.literal: For offending Su Shun he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Su Shun he took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，起原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時軍興餉絀，希蓮條陳開源節流數端，恭親王奕訢韙之。

translations.literal: At the time military expenses had arisen and funds were short; Xilian itemized several proposals to increase revenue and cut expenditure, and Prince Gong Yixin approved them.
translations.idiomatic: With war driving up costs and funds running short, Xilian submitted detailed proposals to raise revenue and cut spending; Prince Gong Yixin endorsed them.

sentences.zh: 雲南報銷案發，同僚有褫職遣戍者，希蓮獨無所染。

translations.literal: When the Yunnan accounts-settlement case broke out, colleagues had their posts stripped and were sent into exile; Xilian alone was not tainted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yunnan accounts scandal broke, colleagues lost their posts and were exiled; Xilian alone emerged untainted.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，出為江西廣饒道，除濫稅，复徵額。

translations.literal: During Guangxu he went out as intendant of the Guangrao Circuit in Jiangxi, eliminated excessive taxes, and restored collection quotas.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era he was posted as intendant of the Guangrao Circuit in Jiangxi, where he abolished illegal levies and restored proper tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 擢山東鹽運使，調長蘆。

translations.literal: He was promoted to salt transport commissioner of Shandong and transferred to Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Shandong salt transport commissioner and transferred to the Changlu salt district.

sentences.zh: 累遷貴州按察使、陝西布政使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 戊戌政變，希蓮頗憂大亂將起，與總督陶模議籌建陪都。

translations.literal: At the coup of 1898 Xilian greatly feared that great disorder was about to arise; with Governor Tao Mo he discussed planning an alternate capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup of 1898 Xilian feared civil collapse was near and discussed with Governor Tao Mo the idea of establishing a secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 及兩宮西幸，入始服其先見雲。

translations.literal: When the two empresses fled west, people then admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowagers fled west, people at last recognized his foresight.

sentences.zh: 李金鏞，字秋亭，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Li Jinyong, styled Qiuting, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinyong, whose courtesy name was Qiuting, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少為賈，以試用同知投效淮軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was a merchant; as a probationary subprefect he joined the Huai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a merchant; later, as a probationary subprefect, he enlisted with the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，淮、徐災，與浙人胡光鏞集十餘萬金往賑，為義賑之始。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, when Huai and Xu suffered disaster, he and the Zhejiang man Hu Guangyong collected more than one hundred thousand taels and went to give relief—the beginning of charitable disaster relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu, when the Huai and Xu regions were stricken, he and Hu Guangyong of Zhejiang raised over one hundred thousand taels for relief—the first organized private charity of its kind.

sentences.zh: 後遂賑直隸、山東，皆躬其役。

translations.literal: Later he went on to give relief in Zhili and Shandong, personally undertaking the work in each case.
translations.idiomatic: He later led relief efforts in Zhili and Shandong as well, personally overseeing the work in each.

sentences.zh: 五年，晉秩知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted in rank to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 調直隸，修西淀堤。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhili, he repaired the Xidian dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhili, he repaired the dikes at Xidian.

sentences.zh: 吳大澂督防吉林，金鏞任琿春招墾事。

translations.literal: When Wu Dacheng supervised the defense of Jilin, Jinyong was put in charge of colonization affairs at Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Dacheng took charge of Jilin's defenses, Jinyong handled colonization at Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 界外蘇城溝墾戶數千，苦俄人侵略，相率來歸，咸得奠居。

translations.literal: Several thousand colonist households at Sucheng Gou beyond the border, suffering Russian aggression, came back together in groups and all obtained settled dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand colonist families at Sucheng Gou beyond the border, harassed by Russian encroachment, returned en masse under his protection and were resettled.

sentences.zh: 海參威既通商，俄人援例要請東三省要地設領事，嚴拒之。

translations.literal: Once Vladivostok was opened to trade, the Russians cited precedent and demanded consulates in key places of the three eastern provinces; he sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Vladivostok opened to trade, the Russians cited precedent to demand consulates at strategic points across the Northeast; he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又力爭八道河民被俄焚掠，抵俄官於法。

translations.literal: He also vigorously contended on behalf of the people of Badao River who had been burned and plundered by Russians, holding Russian officials to account under the law.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought hard for the people of Badao River, whose villages the Russians had burned and looted, pressing the Russian authorities to answer under law.

sentences.zh: 將軍銘安以為才，疏留吉林任用。

translations.literal: General Ming'an considered him talented and memorialized to retain him for service in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: General Ming'an recognized his ability and memorialized the court to keep him in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 中俄界約，自瑚布河口循琿春河至圖門江口，以海中之嶺為界嶺，以西屬中國，距江口二十餘裡立土字碑。

translations.literal: Under the Sino-Russian border treaty, from the mouth of the Huhu River along the Hunchun River to the mouth of the Tumen River, the ridge in the sea was taken as the border ridge; west of it belonged to China, and a boundary marker bearing the character tu was erected more than twenty li from the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sino-Russian treaty the border ran from the Huhu River mouth along the Hunchun to the Tumen estuary, with a ridge in the sea as the dividing line; west of it was Chinese territory, and a boundary marker was set up some twenty li from the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 界圖疏略，致嶺西之罕奇、毛琛崴等鹽場置線外。

translations.literal: The border map was rough and abbreviated, with the result that salt fields west of the ridge such as Hanqi and Maochenwei were placed outside the line.
translations.idiomatic: The border map was imprecise, leaving salt works west of the ridge—Hanqi, Maochenwei, and others—on the wrong side of the line.

sentences.zh: 俄复於黑頂子地私設卡倫，距江口幾百里矣。

translations.literal: The Russians again privately set up barricade posts at Heidingzi, several hundred li from the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Russians then set up unauthorized border posts at Heidingzi, hundreds of li beyond the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 大澂使金鏞會勘，據約爭還侵地，重立界碑。

translations.literal: Dacheng sent Jinyong to conduct a joint survey; relying on the treaty he contested the return of invaded territory and re-erected the boundary markers.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng dispatched Jinyong to conduct a joint survey; citing the treaty he recovered the encroached territory and re-erected the boundary markers.

sentences.zh: 署吉林知府，整錢法，開溝洫，攤丁於地，以蘇民困。

translations.literal: Acting as prefect of Jilin, he reformed the currency system, opened ditches and canals, apportioned labor corvée to land, and thereby relieved the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: As acting prefect of Jilin he reformed the currency, dug irrigation channels, and apportioned corvée duties to landholdings to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 九年，署長春廳通判。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as acting subprefect of Changchun Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as acting subprefect of Changchun.

sentences.zh: 廳境為蒙古郭爾羅斯地，初招流民領墾納租，久之墾逾所領，謂之「夾荒」。

translations.literal: The subprefecture's territory was Mongol Gorlos land; at first migrant settlers were recruited to receive allotments for cultivation and pay rent. After long years the land under cultivation exceeded what had been allotted, and this was called "sandwiched wasteland."
translations.idiomatic: The subprefecture lay on Mongol Gorlos land. Settlers had originally been granted plots to farm and pay rent on, but over time many cleared land beyond their allotments—a practice known as "sandwiched wasteland."

sentences.zh: 民懼增稅，因出錢免丈量，刻石紀之。

translations.literal: The people feared increased taxes and therefore paid money to exempt themselves from land survey; a stone was carved to record the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing higher taxes, the settlers paid a fee to exempt the extra land from survey, and the agreement was carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 至是蒙旗复牒理籓院請丈，金鏞挾碑文謁將軍為民請命，曰：「誠知清丈則公與某各有所得，然如民何？」

translations.literal: At this time the Mongol banner again petitioned the Lifan Yuan to request a survey. Jinyong, taking the stele inscription, visited the general to plead for the people, saying: "I truly know that if a proper survey is carried out, Your Excellency and I will each gain something—but what of the people?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol banner again petitioned the Lifan Yuan for a land survey, Jinyong brought the stele inscription to the general and pleaded on the people's behalf: "I know full well that a proper survey would benefit both Your Excellency and myself—but what becomes of the people?"

sentences.zh: 將軍聞之愕然，奏罷其事。

translations.literal: The general, hearing this, was startled and memorialized to halt the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The general was stunned and memorialized the court to drop the survey.

sentences.zh: 創建書院，厚其廩餼，購書數千卷，資學者誦習。

translations.literal: He founded an academy, enriched its stipends, purchased several thousand volumes of books, and supported scholars in study and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy, increased student stipends, bought several thousand books, and supported local scholars.

sentences.zh: 捕斬劇盜苗青山等，境內乂安。

translations.literal: He captured and executed the notorious bandit Miao Qingshan and others, and peace was restored within the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed the notorious bandit Miao Qingshan and his gang, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 不時巡歷鄉僻，呼召父老，為講孝弟力田。

translations.literal: From time to time he toured remote villages, summoned elders, and lectured them on filial piety, brotherly duty, and diligent farming.
translations.idiomatic: He often toured remote villages, gathering elders to speak on filial duty, neighborliness, and hard work on the land.

sentences.zh: 金鏞性坦易，口操南音，所至民愛而憚之。

translations.literal: Jinyong's nature was frank and easygoing; he spoke with a southern accent. Wherever he went the people loved him yet also stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Frank and unpretentious, with a southern lilt to his speech, Jinyong was loved by the people wherever he served—and feared as well.

sentences.zh: 以功晉道員。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 俄侵占精奇里河四十八旗屯地，在黑龍江岸東。

translations.literal: The Russians occupied the colony lands of forty-eight banners along the Jingqili River, east of the Amur bank.
translations.idiomatic: The Russians seized forty-eight banner colony lands along the Jingqili River, east of the Amur.

sentences.zh: 金鏞爭還補丁屯至老瓜林百七十餘裡，劃河定界。

translations.literal: Jinyong contested the return of supplemental colony settlements as far as Laogualin, more than one hundred seventy li, and fixed the border by delineating the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong recovered supplemental colony lands for more than one hundred seventy li as far as Laogualin, fixing the border along the river.

sentences.zh: 漠河者，在璦琿西，三面界俄，地產金，俄人覬覦之。

translations.literal: Mohe lies west of Aihun, bordered by Russia on three sides; the land produces gold, and the Russians covet it.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe lay west of Aihun, surrounded on three sides by Russian territory. Its gold deposits had long attracted Russian interest.

sentences.zh: 北洋大臣李鴻章議自開採，以金鏞任其事。

translations.literal: Beiyang Minister Li Hongzhang proposed that China open mining itself and assigned Jinyong to the task.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, minister of Beiyang affairs, decided China should mine the region itself and put Jinyong in charge.

sentences.zh: 陸路由墨爾根入，水運由松花江入，各行千餘裡，僻遠無人。

translations.literal: The land route entered by way of Mo'ergen; the water route entered by way of the Songhua River. Each ran more than a thousand li through remote country where no one lived.
translations.idiomatic: The land route ran through Mo'ergen; the water route up the Songhua—each more than a thousand li through empty wilderness.

sentences.zh: 披斬荊棘，於萬山中設三廠，兩年得金三萬。

translations.literal: Clearing thorns and brambles, he established three mines among myriad mountains; in two years he obtained thirty thousand [taels of] gold.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting through wilderness, he opened three mines in the mountains and produced thirty thousand taels of gold in two years.

sentences.zh: 事事與俄關涉，艱阻百端。

translations.literal: Every matter involved the Russians, and difficulties arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Every step brought friction with the Russians; obstacles arose at every turn.

sentences.zh: 又開廠於黑龍江南岸札伊河旁之觀音山，皆為北徼名礦。

translations.literal: He also opened mines at Guanyin Mountain beside the Zhai River on the south bank of the Amur; all were famed northern border mineral sites.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened mines at Guanyin Mountain on the Zhai River south of the Amur—all celebrated frontier deposits.

sentences.zh: 集商貲立公司，流冗遠歸，商販漸集，收實邊之利焉。

translations.literal: He gathered merchant capital to establish a company; wandering unemployed returned from afar, merchants gradually gathered, and he reaped real benefits for the border.
translations.idiomatic: He pooled merchant capital into a company; displaced laborers returned, traders gathered, and the border began to yield real prosperity.

sentences.zh: 十六年，病卒工所。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died of illness at the worksite.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died of illness at the mining site.

sentences.zh: 贈內閣學士，予漠河建祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Secretariat academician, and permission was given to build a temple to him at Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a Grand Secretariat academician, and a memorial shrine was authorized at Mohe.

sentences.zh: 金福曾，字苕人，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Jin Fuceng, styled Tiaoren, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fuceng, whose courtesy name was Tiaoren, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以諸生從軍，先侍祖父衍宗溫州教授，任籌團練助城守。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he joined the army; first he attended his grandfather Yanzong, professor at Wenzhou, and undertook organizing militia to aid in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate who took up arms, he first served under his grandfather Yanzong, a Wenzhou professor, organizing militia to help defend the city.

sentences.zh: 旋隨官兵肅清金、處，協守獨松關，解杭州圍。

translations.literal: Soon he followed government troops in pacifying Jinhua and Chuzhou, jointly guarded Dusong Pass, and lifted the siege of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with imperial forces to pacify Jinhua and Chuzhou, helped hold Dusong Pass, and broke the siege of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章器其才，克蘇州，檄辦善後。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang valued his talent; when Suzhou was taken, he ordered him by dispatch to handle the aftermath.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang valued his ability; after Suzhou fell he put him in charge of reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 捻事起，往贊徐州道張樹聲軍務。

translations.literal: When the Nian rebellion arose, he went to assist Zhang Shusheng, intendant of the Xuzhou Circuit, in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian rebellion broke out he joined Zhang Shusheng, intendant of Xuzhou, in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 捻眾北竄，出防大名。

translations.literal: When Nian bands fled north, he went out to defend Daming.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian rebels drove north he went out to defend Daming.

sentences.zh: 丁憂歸，福曾積功已至知縣，服闋，赴江蘇，歷署婁、南匯、吳江諸邑。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning; Fuceng's accumulated merit had already reached the rank of magistrate. When mourning ended he went to Jiangsu and successively served as acting magistrate of Lou, Nanhui, Wujiang, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he returned to service; by then his accumulated merit had earned him magistrate rank. He went to Jiangsu and served in acting charge of Lou, Nanhui, Wujiang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 所至興學校，課農桑，理冤獄，禁溺女，勸墾沙田，開濬河道，多善政，民有去思。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he established schools, supervised agriculture and sericulture, rectified wrongful cases, forbade female infanticide, encouraged reclaiming tidal flats, and dredged rivers and canals; he had many good policies, and the people felt lingering regret at his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he opened schools, promoted farming and sericulture, righted wrongful convictions, banned female infanticide, encouraged reclamation of tidal land, and dredged waterways. His many good policies left the people sorrowful when he moved on.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，河南、山西大祲。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu, great famine struck Henan and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu years Henan and Shanxi suffered devastating famine.

sentences.zh: 吳人謝家福等倡義賑，集四十餘萬金，推福曾董其事。

translations.literal: The Wu men Xie Jiafu and others initiated charitable relief, collected more than four hundred thousand taels, and recommended Fuceng to direct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jiafu and other philanthropists from Jiangsu raised over four hundred thousand taels for relief and put Fuceng in charge.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，至河南分賑洛陽等十二州縣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year he reached Henan and distributed relief in Luoyang and eleven other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he reached Henan and distributed relief across Luoyang and eleven other prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 新安、澠池災尤重，福曾創立善堂，卹嫠掩骼，收贖子女，購車馬若干輛，代疲民應役。

translations.literal: Disaster was especially severe in Xin'an and Mianchi; Fuceng founded benevolent halls, comforted widows and buried exposed bones, collected and redeemed sold children, purchased several carts and horses, and substituted for exhausted people in corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: Where suffering was worst—in Xin'an and Mianchi—Fuceng opened relief halls, cared for widows, buried the dead, redeemed children sold into servitude, and bought carts and horses so exhausted villagers would not have to perform corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 開渠澗，制龍骨車，興水利。

translations.literal: He opened channels and ravines, made dragon-bone water wheels, and promoted waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He dug channels, built chain-pump water wheels, and revived irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 又濬洛陽、宜陽廢渠，貫通伊、洛，灌田二萬頃。

translations.literal: He also dredged abandoned canals in Luoyang and Yiyang, connected the Yi and Luo rivers, and irrigated twenty thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged abandoned canals at Luoyang and Yiyang, linked the Yi and Luo rivers, and irrigated twenty thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 五年，賑山西虞鄉等十縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he gave relief in ten counties of Shanxi including Yuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he directed relief in ten Shanxi counties, including Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 事竣，移賑直隸。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he moved relief operations to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When that work was done he shifted relief efforts to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時直隸水患方急，持以工代賑之策。

translations.literal: At the time Zhili's water disaster was urgent; he advocated a policy of work in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: With flooding ravaging Zhili, he pushed a work-for-relief policy.

sentences.zh: 七年，疏大清河，濬中亭河，培千里堤。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he dredged the Daqing River, dredged the Zhongting River, and reinforced the Qianli Dike.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he dredged the Daqing and Zhongting rivers and reinforced the Qianli Dike.

sentences.zh: 福曾先援例以道員候選，至是鴻章督直隸，奏留總辦籌賑局。

translations.literal: Fuceng had earlier used precedent to qualify as a candidate for circuit intendant; at this time Hongzhang governed Zhili and memorialized to retain him as chief organizer of the relief planning bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Fuceng had earlier qualified as a circuit intendant candidate by precedent; now, with Li Hongzhang governing Zhili, he was retained to head the relief planning bureau.

sentences.zh: 福曾以淀地淤塞為清河受病之源，清丈東淀無糧地，釐定葦租，規复垡船。

translations.literal: Fuceng held that siltation of the lake district was the source of the Qing River's affliction; he surveyed unregistered land at Dongdian, fixed reed rents, and planned restoration of turf boats.
translations.idiomatic: Fuceng traced the Qing River's chronic flooding to silt choking the lake district; he surveyed unregistered land at Dongdian, set reed rents, and planned to restore turf boats.

sentences.zh: 八年，濬東淀河道，修築天津三河頭堤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he dredged the Dongdian river course and built the dike at Sanhetou in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he dredged the Dongdian waterways and built the Sanhetou dike at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 九年，築子牙河堤，展寬正河，又別開支河王家口以洩盛漲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he built the Ziya River dike, widened the main channel, and separately opened the branch river at Wangjiakou to discharge flood surges.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he built dikes on the Ziya River, widened the main channel, and cut a spillway at Wangjiakou to handle flood peaks.

sentences.zh: 十年，畿東大水，福曾疏青龍灣減河入七里海，疏筐兒港減河入塌河淀，並出北塘海口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year great floods struck east of the capital region; Fuceng dredged the Qinglongwan floodway into Qilihai, dredged the Kuang'er Gang floodway into Tahe Lake, and both discharged at the Beitang estuary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year catastrophic floods hit the capital's eastern districts; Fuceng dredged the Qinglongwan spillway into Qilihai and the Kuang'er Gang spillway into Tahe Lake, both emptying through the Beitang estuary.

sentences.zh: 又開瀝水各河以洩武清、寶坻窪區積水。

translations.literal: He also opened various li-shui rivers to discharge accumulated water in the low areas of Wuqing and Baodi.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened drainage channels to draw off standing water from the lowlands of Wuqing and Baodi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，濬饒陽滹沱河。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he dredged the Hutuo River at Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he dredged the Hutuo River at Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，濬四女寺南運減河。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he dredged the Sinu Temple South Canal floodway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he dredged the Sinu Temple spillway on the South Canal.

sentences.zh: 兩署永定河道，塞決口，於下口別闢新道。

translations.literal: Twice he served as commissioner of the Yongding River; he blocked breach points and at the lower mouth opened a new channel separately.
translations.idiomatic: Twice acting as Yongding River commissioner, he sealed breach points and cut a new channel at the river's lower reach.

sentences.zh: 又就大清河合流處別濬新河，永定河水始直達天津海河。

translations.literal: He also separately dredged a new river at the confluence of the Daqing River, so that Yongding River water could at last reach the Hai River at Tianjin directly.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut a new channel where the Daqing River joined the system, allowing Yongding waters to flow straight to the Hai River at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 山東河決數為災，鴻章輒檄福曾往助工賑，親至蘇、浙募貲。

translations.literal: Shandong river breaches repeatedly caused disasters; Hongzhang always ordered Fuceng by dispatch to go assist with labor and relief, and personally went to Jiangsu and Zhejiang to raise funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong's rivers repeatedly burst their banks, Li Hongzhang repeatedly dispatched Fuceng to oversee relief and labor—and went personally to Jiangsu and Zhejiang to raise funds.

sentences.zh: 會浙西大水，巡撫崧駿复疏留福曾治工賑。

translations.literal: Coinciding with great flood in western Zhejiang, Governor Songjun again memorialized to retain Fuceng to manage works and relief.
translations.idiomatic: When western Zhejiang suffered severe flooding, Governor Songjun again petitioned to keep Fuceng in charge of hydraulic works and relief.

sentences.zh: 於是杭、嘉、湖三府各河次第疏瀹。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various rivers of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou three prefectures were dredged in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou were then dredged one after another.

sentences.zh: 會廷議濬餘杭南湖，以福曾董其役。

translations.literal: The court discussed dredging South Lake at Yuhang, and Fuceng was put in charge of the work.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated dredging South Lake at Yuhang, Fuceng was named to direct the project.

sentences.zh: 明年工竣，直、魯又告災，福曾已臥病，猶力疾籌賑濟。

translations.literal: The next year the work was completed; Zhili and Shandong again reported disaster; Fuceng was already bedridden with illness, yet still forced himself ill to plan relief.
translations.idiomatic: The work finished the following year, but Zhili and Shandong reported new disasters. Though bedridden, Fuceng still forced himself to organize relief.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 鴻章等疏請優恤，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Hongzhang and others memorialized requesting special condolence, and he was posthumously made a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang and others petitioned for special honors; he was posthumously made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 福曾廉公好義，歷辦工賑十餘年，無日不勞身焦思，治行卓然。

translations.literal: Fuceng was upright, public-spirited, and fond of righteousness; for more than ten years he handled works and relief without a day when he did not weary his body and burn his thoughts; his record of governance was outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Fuceng was upright and public-spirited. For more than ten years he ran relief and public works without a day's rest, and his administrative record was outstanding.

sentences.zh: 及其歿，士民同聲惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, scholars and commoners alike voiced regret.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, officials and commoners alike mourned him.

sentences.zh: 熊其英，字純叔，江蘇青浦人。

translations.literal: Xiong Qiying, styled Chunshu, was a native of Qingpu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Qiying, courtesy name Chunshu, was from Qingpu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以貢生就訓導。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he took up the post of instructor.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute student, he became a district instructor.

sentences.zh: 家福集金賑河南，其英請行，始事濟源。

translations.literal: Jiafu gathered funds to relieve Henan; Qiying asked to go and first took up work at Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiafu raised funds for Henan relief, Qiying volunteered and began at Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 濟源山僻小縣也，災尤劇，多方補苴，次第以及他邑。

translations.literal: Jiyuan was a remote mountain county; the disaster was especially severe; he patched relief from many sides and in succession extended to other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan was a remote mountain county hit especially hard; he improvised relief there, then moved on to other districts in turn.

sentences.zh: 其英親履窮僻，稽察戶口，不避風雪，食惟麥粥、麵餅、菜羹，與饑民同苦。

translations.literal: Qiying personally went to remote poor places, examined household registers, did not avoid wind and snow, ate only wheat porridge, wheat cakes, and vegetable soup, and shared hardship with the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying went in person to the poorest villages, checked household registers, braved wind and snow, and ate only porridge, flatbread, and vegetable soup—sharing the hunger of the people he served.

sentences.zh: 初頭病瘍，足病濕，醫少愈，仍從事不肯休，遂卒於衛輝。

translations.literal: At first he suffered head sores and foot dampness; when the doctor had slightly cured him he still continued work and would not rest, and thus died at Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: He developed sores on his head and rheumatism in his feet; though briefly improved by doctors, he refused to stop working and died at Weihui.

sentences.zh: 巡撫上聞，詔許被賑各州縣立祠祀之。

translations.literal: The governor reported upward; by edict the various districts that had received relief were permitted to erect shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The governor reported his death; the throne authorized shrines in every district he had relieved.

sentences.zh: 家福，字綏之，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Jiafu, styled Suizhi, was a native of Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiafu, courtesy name Suizhi, was from Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 世以行善為事。

translations.literal: His family for generations took doing good as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His family had done charitable work for generations.

sentences.zh: 聞豫、晉災，呼籥尤切。

translations.literal: Hearing of disasters in Henan and Shanxi, he cried out with pipes all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of famine in Henan and Shanxi, he appealed urgently for help.

sentences.zh: 義聲傾動，聞者風起。

translations.literal: His righteous reputation shook all sides; those who heard responded like wind rising.
translations.idiomatic: His appeal stirred the region; donors responded in waves.

sentences.zh: 自上海、蘇、揚及杭、湖，原助賑者眾。

translations.literal: From Shanghai, Suzhou, Yangzhou, and Hangzhou and Huzhou, those willing to aid relief were many.
translations.idiomatic: From Shanghai, Suzhou, Yangzhou, Hangzhou, and Huzhou, many came forward to give.

sentences.zh: 日賚錢至家福門，或千金，或數千金，不一年得銀四十三萬有奇。

translations.literal: Each day money was sent to Jiafu's door, sometimes a thousand taels, sometimes several thousand; in less than a year he obtained more than four hundred thirty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Money poured in daily—sometimes a thousand taels, sometimes several thousand. In less than a year he raised more than 430,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 凡賑二十七州，繼其英往者七十四人。

translations.literal: In all he relieved twenty-seven prefectures; seventy-four people followed Qiying to go.
translations.idiomatic: Relief reached twenty-seven prefectures; seventy-four volunteers followed Qiying into the field.

sentences.zh: 家福才識為時重，於創辦電報及推廣招商輸船局事多所策畫。

translations.literal: Jiafu's talent and insight were valued by the age; in founding the telegraph and expanding the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company he contributed many plans.
translations.idiomatic: Jiafu's ability was widely respected; he helped plan the telegraph service and the expansion of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章尤賞之，嘗疏薦稱有「物與民胞」之量，體國經野之才。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang especially prized him and once memorialized recommending him as having the breadth of 'all creatures and the people as one body' and talent for ordering the state and governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang especially valued him and once recommended him as a man with compassion for all people and talent for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 金福曾亦聞而歎許焉。

translations.literal: Jin Fuceng also heard and sighed in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fuceng, hearing of him, also expressed admiration.

sentences.zh: 家福歷保至直隸州知州，卒不仕。

translations.literal: Jiafu was repeatedly recommended up to Zhili department magistrate, but in the end did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiafu was repeatedly recommended for office up to Zhili department magistrate but never served.

sentences.zh: 時又有吳江紳富沈中堅，鬻田三十頃，親往山西賑災。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the Wujiang gentry wealthy man Shen Zhongjian, who sold thirty qing of fields and personally went to Shanxi to relieve disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shen Zhongjian, a wealthy gentleman of Wujiang, sold thirty qing of land and went personally to Shanxi to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 亦義行之尤著者。

translations.literal: He was also among those whose righteous conduct was especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He too was noted for outstanding charitable deeds.

sentences.zh: 童兆蓉，字少芙，湖南寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Tong Zhaorong, styled Shaofu, was a native of Ningxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Zhaorong, courtesy name Shaofu, was from Ningxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治六年舉人，從軍陝西，積功晉知府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he became a provincial graduate, followed the army in Shaanxi, and by accumulated merit was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of the sixth year of Tongzhi, he campaigned in Shaanxi and rose to prefect by merit.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，署榆林。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he served as acting magistrate of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he acted as magistrate of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，便宜發倉，復運粟於包頭、寧夏，單騎臨賑。

translations.literal: In a year of crop failure he expediently opened granaries, also transported grain from Baotou and Ningxia, and alone on horseback went to oversee relief.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he opened granaries on his own authority, brought grain from Baotou and Ningxia, and rode alone to supervise relief.

sentences.zh: 既而大疫，延榆綏道及榆林令皆遽歿，代者不至。

translations.literal: Before long a great epidemic came; the Yan-Yulin-Suide circuit intendant and the Yulin magistrate all suddenly died, and replacements did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a plague struck; the circuit intendant and the Yulin magistrate died suddenly, and no replacements arrived.

sentences.zh: 兆蓉一身兼攝三官，比戶存問，為具醫藥，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Zhaorong alone held three offices concurrently, inquired after every household, provided medicine, and preserved alive very many.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaorong held three offices alone, visited every household, supplied medicine, and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 六年，署延榆綏道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting Yan-Yulin-Suide circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he acted as Yan-Yulin-Suide circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 屬郡荒僻，土僿民貧。

translations.literal: The subordinate prefectures were remote and desolate, the soil poor and the people impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction was remote, the soil poor, and the people impoverished.

sentences.zh: 為拓學舍，購書勸課，教民樹藝畜牧。

translations.literal: He expanded schoolhouses, purchased books and urged instruction, and taught the people planting, crafts, and animal husbandry.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded schools, bought books, encouraged study, and taught farming and animal husbandry.

sentences.zh: 治榆溪河，開渠溉田，民利之。

translations.literal: He regulated the Yuxi River, opened canals to irrigate fields, and the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated the Yuxi River, dug irrigation canals, and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 八年，授興安知府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed prefect of Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed prefect of Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 汰胥役，禁私錢。

translations.literal: He eliminated clerks and runners and forbade private coin.
translations.idiomatic: He purged corrupt clerks and banned private coinage.

sentences.zh: 總兵餘虎恩販錢為利，獲而毀之。

translations.literal: Brigadier Yu Hu'en profited from selling coin; he seized and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and destroyed counterfeit coin sold for profit by Brigadier Yu Hu'en.

sentences.zh: 稅胥索賈人金，榜治幾死。

translations.literal: A tax clerk demanded gold from a merchant; he had him beaten nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: When a tax clerk extorted a merchant, he had the man flogged nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 民間婚娶苟簡，為定禮制，禁淫祀，葺昭忠、節孝祠，以正民志。

translations.literal: Popular weddings and funerals were careless and simple; he set ritual regulations, forbade improper sacrifices, repaired shrines to loyal martyrs and chaste women, to correct popular aims.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated weddings and funerals, banned improper cults, and restored shrines to loyal martyrs and chaste women to guide public morals.

sentences.zh: 安康令徵糧苛急，民聚而譁，兆蓉往撫諭。

translations.literal: The Ankang magistrate pressed grain collection harshly; the people gathered and clamored; Zhaorong went to soothe and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ankang magistrate pressed grain collection too hard and the people rioted, Zhaorong went to calm them.

sentences.zh: 總兵及釐局挾前嫌，誣為激變，遂解任。

translations.literal: The brigadier and the transit-tax bureau, holding prior grudges, falsely accused him of inciting disturbance, and he was then removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The brigadier and transit-tax bureau, nursing old grudges, falsely accused him of inciting riot, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋得白，署漢中，逾年還本任。

translations.literal: Soon he was cleared; he served as acting at Hanzhong, and after a year returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon cleared, acted at Hanzhong, and returned to his post after a year.

sentences.zh: 川匪擾境，擒斬其渠，賊潰走。

translations.literal: Sichuan bandits disturbed the border; he captured and beheaded their chief, and the bandits collapsed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan rebels raided the border, he captured and executed their leader and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 調西安，攝督糧道，定徵糧改折，上下稱便。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xi'an, acted as grain-supply commissioner, fixed grain collection with conversion payments, and above and below all called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Xi'an, he acted as grain commissioner and fixed a commutation system for tax grain that officials and people alike found convenient.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢浙江溫處道，先署杭嘉湖，明年乃之任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Wen-Chu Circuit in Zhejiang, first acted at Hang-Jia-Hu, and the next year then went to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to the Wen-Chu circuit in Zhejiang, first acting at Hang-Jia-Hu, and took up the post the following year.

sentences.zh: 值拳匪亂後，瑞安民楊茂奶與教堂積釁。

translations.literal: He encountered the period after the Boxer turmoil; Yang Maonai of Ruian and the church had accumulated grievances.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer uprising, Yang Maonai of Ruian and the local church had long-standing grievances.

sentences.zh: 浙東法國主教趙保祿尤橫，挾兵船至溫州，必欲殺楊。

translations.literal: The French bishop of eastern Zhejiang, Zhao Baolu, was especially overbearing; he brought warships to Wenzhou and insisted on killing Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Bishop Zhao Baolu of eastern Zhejiang was especially domineering; he brought gunboats to Wenzhou and demanded Yang's execution.

sentences.zh: 兆蓉力爭曰：「彼法不當死，我不能殺人以媚人。」

translations.literal: Zhaorong strove against it, saying: 'By law he ought not die; I cannot kill a man to please others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaorong argued firmly: 'He does not deserve death under the law. I will not execute a man to please foreigners.

sentences.zh: 卒拒之，以此名聞。

translations.literal: In the end he refused, and by this his name became known.
translations.idiomatic: He refused in the end, and won renown for it.

sentences.zh: 颶風為災，賑糶並舉，民不乏食。

translations.literal: A typhoon caused disaster; relief and grain sales were undertaken together, and the people did not lack food.
translations.idiomatic: When a typhoon struck, he ran relief and grain sales together so the people did not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光緒初，各省重吏治，監司大吏下逮守令，皆一時之選。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Early in Guangxu each province emphasized official governance; provincial supervisors and great officials down to magistrates were all selections of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: Early in the Guangxu era the provinces stressed good government; from provincial supervisors down to district magistrates, the appointments were men of real ability.

sentences.zh: 朝儀以下諸人，或禦亂保民，或治盜清訟，或興學勸業，或救災卹患，莫不以民生為重。

translations.literal: Chaoyi and the others below, some quelled disorder and protected the people, some governed bandits and cleared lawsuits, some promoted schools and urged industry, some relieved disaster and succored calamity—none did not take the people's livelihood as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: From Chaoyi downward, some quelled rebellion and protected the people, some suppressed banditry and cleared the courts, some promoted schools and industry, some relieved famine and disaster—all put the people's welfare first.

sentences.zh: 承兵燹後，辛苦凋殘之人，得生存以至今日者，實賴於此。

translations.literal: Inheriting the period after warfare and conflagration, those who toiled in hardship and devastation and were able to survive until today in truth relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars, the exhausted survivors who reached the present day owed their lives in large part to such men.

sentences.zh: 「民亦勞止，汔可小休，惠此中國，以為民逑」。

translations.literal: 'The people also have labored long; surely they may rest a little; show favor to this central kingdom, and be the people's guide.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The people too have labored long; may they now rest a little. Show grace to this central land and be a true guide to the people.'

sentences.zh: 誠知本哉！

translations.literal: Truly one knows the root!
translations.idiomatic: This indeed is the root of governance!

sentences.zh: [一]按：劉含芳傳所附陳黌舉傳，關內本與關外一次本無。

translations.literal: Note: The biography of Chen Hongju appended to the biography of Liu Hanfang is absent from both the inside-the-pass and outside-the-pass first editions.
translations.idiomatic: Editor's note: The biography of Chen Hongju appended to Liu Hanfang's biography does not appear in either the inside-the-pass or outside-the-pass first editions.
